# Cadence — task list

The running record of work: open, in progress, done, cancelled. Started 2026-08-16.

**Format.** One line per item: `- [id] Title — note`. Ids are stable and never reused, so a
cancelled or done item can still be referenced later. Done items keep their commit sha, because the
commit message is where the *reasoning* lives; this file is only the index.

**Rule (set 2026-08-17).** *Every* request the user makes lands here the moment it is made, whether
or not work starts on it — under **In progress** if it is being worked now, otherwise under the
right Open section. An item moves to **Done** only when the code behind it is committed (or
otherwise verified), not when it is written.

**Target devices** (set 2026-08-16). Build and verify for these three only; anything that exists
solely to serve other hardware is dead weight and should be removed rather than maintained:

| Device | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone 15 (base) | 393 × 852 | compact width, the only phone shape that matters |
| iPad Pro 11" | 834 × 1210 portrait · 1210 × 834 landscape | pane = window − 188pt sidebar → **646** portrait, **1022** landscape |
| MacBook Pro 14" | 1512 × 982 | the macOS surface |

Both iPad panes matter to Today's layout: 646pt portrait falls **below**
`CadenceTodayLayoutSupport.twoPaneMinimumWidth` (761), so portrait is one column and landscape is
two. The three-pane floor of 1022pt that this note used to cite is gone with the layout itself
(T-06).

- [T-7551] **CLOSED 2026-10-27 (agent `tlscroll1300`, the commit carrying this line; SEEN ON SCREEN on `Cadence-iPadPro11` -- a swipe begun on a standing draft now scrolls the timeline and leaves the draft exactly as it was) -- the draft block's two SwiftUI drags are gone: the edge handle holds before it adjusts, and the adjustment observer does not exist any more because the handle reports its own.** The owner ranked the two symptoms when they read [[T-7550]]: *"the draft collapsing is worse than the scrolling."* That is right -- a swipe silently destroying 45 minutes of a block just drawn is data loss, where failing to scroll is an annoyance -- and it is the half this fix is built around. **Both offenders are gone, and they needed different answers.** (1) `iOSTimelineDraftCreate.swift` `edgeHandle` was a `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 1)` over a 32pt band that is most of a one-hour draft plus 14pt of plain canvas past each end, so it answered every finger that landed on it; it is now `iOSTimelinePressDrag` at `CadenceTimelineBlockEdit.liftPressDuration`, the figure every other time edit on this canvas already uses. **The axis test was considered and is wrong here, which is why it was not taken:** `iOSRowHorizontalPanRecognizer` separates a row swipe from a scroll by DIRECTION, and an edge adjustment is a *vertical* drag competing with a *vertical* scroll -- they are not separable by direction at all, only in TIME. `minimumDistance` is not an option; [[T-2059]] measured it dead for this exact collision. **The cost, stated rather than hidden:** an adjustment no longer begins the instant the finger lands, which is a real loss of immediacy on a small target. The failure it replaces destroyed 45 minutes silently; the one it introduces is that a flick aimed at the handle scrolls instead, costing a second try. A cancelled adjustment now also puts the edge back, which the `DragGesture` could not -- a SwiftUI gesture the system cancels never reaches `onEnded`, so it left the edge wherever the last callback had dragged it. (2) `draftAdjustmentObserver` was a `.simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 1))` on the WHOLE draft block that moved nothing -- it captured the draft's range on touch-down and compared it on release, to tell an edge adjustment apart from a scroll ([[T-3246]]). A SwiftUI drag cannot watch without taking, so it claimed every touch on the draft, and it was inferring from the outside a thing the handle knew for certain. **It is deleted, not converted**: the handle calls `restoreDraftEditorAfterAdjustment()` once, at the end of its own drag, behind its own `guard landed != anchor`. T-3246's invariant survives exactly -- only a touch that moved an edge puts the editor back -- as a fact rather than an inference, with no captured range (`draftRangeUnderTouch` is gone) to go stale. **Measured on `Cadence-iPadPro11` with injected finger touch paths, never scroll-wheel events:** a 300pt swipe begun squarely in a 3-4 PM draft's bottom handle band scrolled the pane 6 AM -> 12 AM and left the draft at **3 PM - 4 PM**, against the same swipe before the fix which scrolled zero and collapsed a 4:45-5:45 PM draft to 4:45-5:00; then a hold-and-drag on that handle took a 7:30-8:30 AM draft to **7:30 - 9:15 AM** and the editor came back by itself with the keyboard DOWN, which is `.returnedAfterAdjustment` and so proves the restore fired from the handle and not from the canvas tap. **[[T-7550]] re-checked on the same build and not regressed:** scroll from empty canvas (12 AM -> 6 AM), long-press move a committed block (5-7:15 PM -> 4-6:15 PM), tap to open (`Today - 4 PM - 2h 15m`), press-drag sizing at create (`Estimate 2h`), the lifted block's own edge handle (4-6:15 PM -> 4-7 PM), two-finger pinch out and back; - [T-7512] **OPEN 2026-10-27 (agent `dataint1200`, filed with [[T-6482]]'s fix; read against source, NOT run) -- [[T-6482]]'s import gate narrows the stranding window; it does not close it, and no local signal can.** The deferred merges run on the first mirroring import of the launch that reports `endDate != nil` and `succeeded`. A first sync arrives in **batches** -- that import is one of several -- and a push can bring a child of a merged-away row at any later moment in the session or in a later session that reaches the gate sooner. `NSPersistentCloudKitContainer` exposes no "converged" signal, and the re-pointing fix [[T-6482]] rejected is impossible on this schema: `Subtask.parentTask`, `FocusSessionLog.task/area/project` and `AppTask.area/project/goal/context` are relationships with **no stored id beside them**, so a child that arrives orphaned carries no record of which parent it wanted. Closing the hole therefore needs a schema change (a scalar parent id on those four models, written by this build onward) plus a durable merged-away-id -> survivor-id map, and it would still do nothing for rows already written by every shipped build. Owner decision, not an oversight: do not re-file as a bug. Size L if ever taken.

RC-TRIAGE: N/A -- agent tooling, nothing a user sees, but it corrupts RC verification evidence, so it is worth doing before the next frozen-export run.

- [T-5561] **CLOSED 2026-10-24 declined by OWNER DECISION** (recorded by the coordinator in the commit carrying this line; no code changed, nothing built) -- option (a), LEAVE THE RANKING. A list's documents go on ranking below that list's tasks, with the Notes section last. The question this entry asked was the second reading of "lists first, then tasks", and the owner's answer is that the first reading is the one that was meant: discovery already works, nothing is broken, and both alternatives on offer (list documents in their own section above Tasks, or the whole Notes section above Tasks) would have contradicted the same decision's "not one-section-per-kind" clause. The entry is closed as answered, not as implemented -- there is nothing to implement. -- previously **OPEN 2026-10-23 (agent `macsearch`, the commit carrying this line; found while landing [[T-3084]]'s second half) -- the owner's "lists first, then tasks" has a second reading that [[T-3084]] did not implement: should a list DOCUMENT rank above tasks, and if so, where?** The decision as recorded reads "**lists first, then tasks.** Containers rank above their contents, so searching a list's name returns the list as the top hit rather than burying it under thirty of its own tasks. Not one-section-per-kind." [[T-3084]] implemented the reasoning sentence literally: a CONTAINER is an Area or a Project, its CONTENTS are its tasks, and `buildIndexedSource` already orders Areas and Projects before Tasks -- now pinned by `CadenceMacListDocumentSearchTests.containersRankAboveTheirContents`, which dies if that order moves. **The other reading is that the new list-document rows themselves belong above Tasks.** A list document is not a container of tasks, so the reasoning sentence does not reach it; but the palette's Notes section is drawn LAST, after Tasks, so a list document matching the same query as fourteen of its list's tasks is listed below all of them. **Why this is an owner question and not an implementer's call:** the palette is a fixed sequence of per-category sections (`GlobalSearchIndexSupport.buildIndexedSource` appends Commands, Pages, Areas, Projects, Tasks, Calendar Events, Event Notes, Notes, and `GlobalSearchOverlayStateSupport.keyboardRows` walks them in that order). Lifting list documents above Tasks therefore needs EITHER a new section ordered before `.tasks` -- which is the one-section-per-kind the same decision rules out -- OR moving the whole Notes section above Tasks, which would move Daily, Weekly and Notepad rows too, a visible change to four kinds that nobody asked for. **What is wanted here is one answer, not a design:** (a) leave it as landed -- list documents sit in the Notes section, containers stay above their contents; (b) list documents get their own section above Tasks, accepting the per-kind section; or (c) the whole Notes section moves above Tasks, accepting that the other four kinds move with it. Nothing is broken either way -- this is ranking, not discovery, and discovery works. Filed rather than guessed because the decision says the ranking is "explicitly not left to the implementer".

  **4. What was deliberately NOT removed, each with its reason.** (a) The context/area/project **merges'** re-pointing of `goal.context` / `habit.context` in `DataIntegrityRepairService`: it fires only when a duplicate `Context` already exists and is about to be deleted, and it moves a surviving goal or habit onto the canonical row instead of letting the delete nullify its filing — removing it would make this ticket *lose* data on the rows it exists to preserve. - [T-1115] **CLOSED 2026-09-09 (agent `weekkeytz`, landed by the coordinator) — `weekKey` reads the caller's time zone, so the pair round-trips at every longitude.** Originally filed as: `DateFormatters.weekKey(from:)` reads the *device's* time zone while
  `weekStartDate(forWeekKey:calendar:)` reads the *caller's*, so the pair only round-trips east of
  UTC.** Filed by `weekkeytz` 2026-09-08 at `8c45c91`, where a full `-only-testing:CadenceTests` run

  `WeekKeyResolutionTests.everyWeekKeyRoundTripsBackIntoItsOwnWeek`, and every one the same shape:
  `(DateFormatters.weekKey(from: monday) → "2025-W52") == (key → "2026-W01")`. Off by exactly one
  week, all 400 iterations. Two findings, and the second is the more expensive one.
  **1. The API asymmetry.** `weekStartDate(forWeekKey:calendar:)` sets `iso.timeZone =
  calendar.timeZone` — deliberate, and the whole point of `c424f42`. `weekKey(from:)` builds its own
  `Calendar(identifier: .iso8601)` two declarations above and **never sets a time zone**, so it
  silently takes the device's. Hand it the Monday-00:00-**UTC** that `weekStartDate` just returned
  for a UTC calendar and a Mac west of UTC calls that instant *Sunday*, i.e. the previous ISO week.
  Measured here by direct computation outside the test host, mirroring both helpers: 400/400
  mismatches under `America/Los_Angeles` and `America/New_York`, **0/400** under `Asia/Shanghai`,
  `Europe/London` (BST) and `Pacific/Auckland`.

  changed between the green runs and this red one; the Mac's time zone did. `c424f42` was authored
  at `+0800`, where the round-trip is exact, so the test recorded the sum of a real API asymmetry and
  the author's longitude and reported it as a pass. A test that only passes east of UTC is an
  instrument blind to its own environment — it was never measuring the property it names. Note also
  that `TZ=…` does **not** reach the spawned macOS test host: `TZ=Asia/Shanghai` and
  `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` produce byte-identical 400-failure runs, so the zone cannot be varied
  from the outside and the correction has to be that both halves take a calendar.
  **Not a user-facing defect, verified rather than assumed.** `DateFormatters.ymd` pins a locale and
  no time zone, so `date(from:)` parses to *local* midnight; every shipping caller of the week
  helpers therefore stands in the device zone on both sides and agrees with itself. Enumerated at
  `8c45c91`: `NotesView.swift:262`, `CadenceNoteDateNavigation.weekRangeLabel`/`weekKey(forDayKey:)`,
  `CadenceNotesListSupport:356`, `CadenceMCPServiceSupport:40`, and `currentWeekKey()` — every one
  takes the `.current` default, and the two declarations that *do* accept a `calendar:`
  (`CadenceNoteDateNavigation.title`, `weekRangeLabel`) are never handed a non-current one outside
  the tests. **This matters because `weekKey` output is persisted** (`Note.weekKey`,
  `WeeklyNote.weekKey`) and syncs through CloudKit, in Production since 2026-09-05: no stored key may
  change meaning, so the fix must be default-preserving.
  **The fix:** give `weekKey` the courtesy `weekStartDate` already has —
  `weekKey(from:calendar: Calendar = .current)` setting `cal.timeZone = calendar.timeZone` — and have
  the test pass its `utc` calendar to both halves of the round-trip.

That is `zsh` reading a script incrementally by byte offset into one open fd, and it is exactly `xcb-widgetdrop-tests` re-running its whole test phase. **It happened a SECOND time, to this entry's own cause.** `1d8786cd`'s author appended ~60 lines to `scripts/xcb.sh` at 01:52 while their own verification run was in postflight; that run had already printed its complete `== xcb result ==` block and was found 40 minutes later executing `test-host-lock.sh acquire` **as a child of itself**, holding the test-host lock and queued behind it at the same time, with `uiseed` and `precheck` stuck behind that. Killed, the lease reclaimed on owner-death, and `uiseed` took the lock 16 seconds later. **THE FIX IS THE ONE THIS ENTRY SUGGESTED**, at the top of `scripts/xcb.sh`: the runner copies itself to `${TMPDIR}cadence-xcb-self.<pid>.<n>.zsh`, re-execs from the copy, and **unlinks the copy immediately** — the fd stays valid (probed), so there is no path left for anyone to edit and no litter either. `exec` keeps the pid, which is what the log name and the lock ticket are keyed on, and `SCRIPT_PATH`/`ROOT_DIR` are carried across explicitly so `$here` and `$ROOT_DIR/scripts/test-host-lock.sh` keep naming the real checkout. It **fails open**: a runner that will not start because it could not copy itself would be worse than one that can be edited underneath it. **PROVED BY INDUCING THE REAL FAILURE, WITH THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT EVIDENCE.** `xcb.sh selftest` section 14 (6 checks; 209 → 215 total, all green) starts a real `xcb.sh <id> test` against stubs and, while it is inside xcodebuild, **truncates and rewrites its own script file in place** with ~900 KB of injected program — far longer than the script, so the read offset cannot land past EOF. Guarded: no injected text, exactly ONE `== xcb result` block, postflight reached, no snapshot left behind, and **no zsh diagnostic naming its own script**. The CONTROL is the same scenario with the guard switched off, and it really does corrupt — it printed `…/ctl/scripts/xcb.sh:21756: unmatched "`, the same shape as `widgetdrop`'s `./scripts/xcb.sh:3336: command not found: the`. Mutating the guard away kills the diagnostic check. **AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE LESSON, which this entry does not state and which every agent needs: HOW you write the file decides whether this can happen at all.** `open(path, "w")` and an in-place editor truncate the SAME inode, which is what hijacks a running shell; writing a temp file on the same filesystem and `mv`-ing it over the target is a rename, leaves the running process's inode untouched, and is atomic. Measured both ways in one probe: the in-place form made the running script execute 36 foreign lines, the rename form left it printing its own three. **Every edit to `scripts/xcb.sh` in this commit was installed by rename while `uiseed` was executing the old copy, and `uiseed` was unaffected.**

- [T-8141] **CLOSED 2026-10-28 (agent `ipaddrag1050`, the commit carrying this line; SEEN ON SCREEN on `Cadence-iPadPro11` both before and after, scope re-checked on `Cadence-iPhone15`; macOS `CadenceTests` run plus the mandatory iOS leg, 0 warnings on both) -- a task row in iPad Today now presses, lifts and lands on the Timeline pane beside it, and the SAME press opens the row's context menu, which had been dead on BOTH form factors since [[T-2059]].** Owner's report: *"on ipad os at least, if i want to drag a task in today's view onto the calendar, it doesnt work. it doesnt drag at all."* **What I saw before:** a 0.8 s press on "[Sample] Overdue launch checklist item" in Today's left column followed by a drag onto the Timeline moved nothing at all -- no lift, no preview, no highlight, no change -- and a 1.3 s STILL press on the same row opened no context menu either, although `iOSTaskRow` has carried `.contextMenu` all along. **What I saw after:** the same press-and-drag leaves the row, follows the finger and lands as a block at 11:30 AM -- 12:30 PM on the Timeline, and Today's header count goes `3 timed` to `4 timed`; the still press opens Edit / Focus / Priority / Repeat / Do Date / Due Date / Move Section / Move to List / Duplicate / Delete Task. **The cause, isolated by differential over four builds rather than by reading:** (1) baseline as above; (2) `.draggable` added to the row and nothing else -- still nothing, so a missing payload was not the cause; (3) `.iOSSwipeActions` removed from the row -- the context menu opened every time and the row lifted, so the swipe container was the blocker; (4) inside the container, `iOSRowHorizontalPanRecognizer`'s `gestureRecognizer(_:shouldBeRequiredToFailBy:)` forced to `false` -- the menu opened with the container still on. That one delegate method is the whole of it (`Cadence/iOS/iOSSwipeActionRow.swift`, added by [[T-2059]] in `02f7c267`): it returns `!(other is UIPanGestureRecognizer)`, i.e. EVERY non-pan recognizer must wait for this one to fail, and a still finger never reaches the axis test, so the recognizer stays `.possible` until touch-up and the wait never ends. Narrowing it by class was tried in between and measured NOT to work -- excluding `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` as well changed nothing on screen, because the recognizers SwiftUI installs for a drag lift and for a context menu are not that class. **Fix:** `CadenceSwipeActionSupport.stillPressYieldSeconds` + `yieldsStillPress(claim:elapsed:)`, armed by `iOSRowHorizontalPanRecognizer.scheduleStillPressYield()` from `touchesBegan` -- an undecided pan fails itself before the system's own press duration, so the lift and the menu fire on time, while a drag that turns horizontal inside the window still claims the row. [[T-2059]]'s own fix is unspent: a vertical drag begun on a task row still scrolls the page, measured on `Cadence-iPhone15` after the change, and the swipe tray still opens on the iPad. Drag source: `.draggable(TaskDragPayload.string(for: task.id))` on `iOSTaskRow`, the same wire format the iOS Calendar Board card already offers. Drop: `iOSCalendarTimelineDayColumn` gains `.dropDestination(for: String.self)` resolving the minute through `CadenceScheduleSupport.timelineMinute`, and BOTH grid hosts (`iOSTodaySchedulePanel`, `iOSCalendarView`) pass a non-optional `onDropTaskAtMinute` through to `CadenceTimelineBlockEdit.commitDrop`, which writes the day AND the minute in one `CadenceTaskFieldEditCommit` transaction -- the parameter has no default precisely because [[T-8091]] is this wiring one host short. **Scope:** the long-press block is in the shared row, so the dead context menu was on iPhone too (seen dead, then seen working, on `Cadence-iPhone15`); the Today-to-Timeline drag itself is iPad-only, because compact Today has no timeline pane. Touch was what I drove; a trackpad/pointer path was NOT exercised. **This also answers the owner's second report** -- that long-press does not open the task menu on iPad while right-click does -- it is the same single cause and needs no separate design; UIKit negotiates hold-still-for-the-menu against hold-and-move-to-drag by itself once nothing is blocking the lift. Tests: `CadenceIOSTaskRowDragLiftTests` (10 tests: the yield's rule and its relation to the system press duration, the drop's day+minute write and its refusal rollback, the id resolver, and four source-wiring scans). Mutation (`scripts/mutate.sh --tree` over a `git archive HEAD` export plus this change): 9/9 KILLED, 0 survived, 0 inconclusive, each one compiled and ran (11 test result lines, 0 warnings) -- including the negative that actually bit, the yield method declared but never armed from `touchesBegan`, which shipped to the simulator for one build with the menu still dead. Residuals filed rather than fixed: [[T-8142]], [[T-8143]].

- [T-8201] **OPEN 2026-10-28 (coordinator `coord1050`, the commit carrying this line; OWNER DECISION, recorded from the owner's words in session; the rule itself is now in `AGENTS.md` under Non-Negotiable Patterns, which is where agents will actually read it -- this entry is the record of WHY, not the rule's home) -- macOS and iOS are ONE app on two platforms: a surface may differ only where hardware or input forces it, and anything that is merely UI is the same on both.** The owner's words: "i want the app on ios and mac os to be essentially the same app, just on two different platforms and hence features related to the difference in platforms can differ. for example, if a feature/ui depends on the screen width or the usage of a mouse or keyboard shortcuts, they may differ in the 2 platforms, but if something is just ui and has little to do with inherit hardware constraints, that feature/ui should stay the same across platforms". **The test to apply:** a platform difference must be justifiable in one sentence naming the hardware or input constraint it answers -- pointer vs touch, hover, right-click, keyboard shortcut, screen width, or a presentation model one platform lacks. If no such sentence exists, it is drift and it gets unified, and the fix is one shared component rather than a second copy nudged closer by hand. This EXTENDS the existing iPhone/iPad line in the same list to the macOS/iOS pair. **What it already settles, so these are no longer open questions:** (a) the completed-task look on the calendar -- macOS's diagonal stripes + green check versus iOS's strikethrough is pure UI with no hardware basis, so it unifies (the owner has separately asked for the macOS look); (b) the task completion animation, pure UI, so iOS gets it; (c) the Kanban card, already being unified under [[T-8181]]; (d) the task and event editors -- the four already share `CadenceSchedulePanel`, so the FIELD SET is not in question, and what remains splits cleanly: the section chrome (iOS's `iOSEditorSection` vocabulary versus macOS's `CadenceFieldSection`) is pure UI and unifies toward the iOS style the owner asked for, while the CONTAINER (a pointer-anchored popover versus a detented sheet) is input-shaped and legitimately differs. **What the rule does NOT erase, because each names its constraint:** the macOS popover's plain notes field, since a popover that presents a sheet from inside itself is a presentation knot (`Cadence/Shared/Components/CadenceSchedulePanel.swift:782-789`) -- a presentation-model constraint; macOS board chips being pickers while iOS chips are labels (`Cadence/iOS/iOSBoardCards.swift:296-299`) -- a tappable region inside a tappable card competes on touch but not under a pointer; the macOS bare-UUID drag payload (`Cadence/Shared/TaskDragPayload.swift:44-49`); and the macOS hover-underline tokens of [[T-8181]], which answer "pointer" exactly. **Standing instruction for audits:** a visible-defect audit may now file cross-platform drift as a defect in its own right, naming the surface and the missing constraint sentence, rather than treating each platform's look as independently correct. RC-TRIAGE: POST-RC, a standing design rule.

- [T-8161] **CLOSED 2026-10-29 (agent `onenote1250`, the commit carrying this line; the owner decision below is unchanged and was filed 2026-10-28 by coordinator `coord1050`; a full macOS `CadenceTests` run green but for the one list this change had to update -- `CadenceTagChipScaleTests`'s declared control callers -- re-run scoped and green after it; iOS leg green; 0 warnings on both; 9/9 mutations KILLED; seen on an iPad simulator, NOT seen on macOS -- see the addendum) -- the event editor gets ONE Notes field, backed by the rich Cadence `Note` (`kind == .meeting`), which mirrors a FLATTENED plain-text copy into `EKEvent.notes`; images stay Cadence-only.** The owner's words: "Keep the rich Cadence note as the single Notes field -- it mirrors a flattened copy to Apple Calendar, and images stay Cadence-only." This replaces today's two surfaces -- iOS `iOSCalendarEventEditSheet.eventNoteSection` (`Cadence/iOS/iOSCalendarEventEditSheet.swift:292`, the "Event Note" Create/Open card) and `notesSection` (`:321`, the "Apple Calendar note" markdown well) -- with one. macOS's equivalents are `linkedNoteCard` (`Cadence/macOS/Views/TimelineEventBlockSupportViews.swift:408`) and `CadenceSchedulePanelNotesRow` (`:237`). Most of the plumbing exists: `CadenceEventNoteSupport.commitNote(syncToCalendar:save:syncToNativeEvent:)` (`Cadence/Shared/CadenceEventNoteSupport.swift:378`) already saves locally FIRST and mirrors only if the local save landed (T-325), and `CadenceEventNoteCommitOutcome.savedButNotSynced` already carries the user sentence "This note is saved, but Apple Calendar didn't take the change." **DERIVED RULES, decided by the coordinator under the owner's ruling -- follow these unless the owner overrides:** (1) mirror ONLY when the Cadence note actually changed, so an edit made in Apple Calendar survives unless the user touches the Cadence note -- this is what stops a silent clobber, since the note today is seeded from `EKEvent.notes` once at creation (`initialContent(eventTitle:nativeNotes:)`, `:292`) and never re-read; (2) the flattened copy is the markdown source as written, minus image references -- `[[note]]` and `[[task:...]]` spans stay as literal text, which reads acceptably in Apple Calendar and round-trips harmlessly; (3) images stay insertable in the merged field, because it IS the rich note and `CadenceMarkdownSourceInventory` still sees them through the `Note` row -- only the mirror drops them, so T-422's `allowsImageInsertion: false` on the Apple Calendar field is retired rather than extended; (4) an event with no Cadence note but with existing `EKEvent.notes` shows that text in the field, and the first edit seeds the `Note` from it -- today's behaviour, kept, and it is what gives the owner "events with existing apple calendar notes will also display their content inside cadence"; (5) on a read-only calendar (`EKCalendar.allowsContentModifications == false`) the `Note` stays editable, the mirror is skipped and the field says so quietly -- the existing carve-out, which is the only reason the split survives cleanly today; (6) MIGRATION, and the one place silent data loss is possible: an event that today has BOTH a Cadence note and DIFFERENT text in `EKEvent.notes` must have the Apple text appended under a divider, never discarded; (7) scope stays per-occurrence (`EKSpan.thisEvent`), matching the mirror today (`CalendarManager.swift:631`, `iOSCalendarManager.swift:300`) and the note's own `#occurrence=` key (`CadenceEventNoteSupport.swift:78`) -- NOT the series, and NOT the `confirmationDialog` a full event edit raises. **STILL OPEN, deliberately:** a continuous read-back of `EKEvent.notes` after note creation. Rule (1) makes external edits survive, but nothing yet makes them WIN, so an Apple-side edit made after a Cadence-side edit is still dropped on the next mirror. iOS has a partial precedent in `reloadEventNotesIfUntouched()` (`iOSCalendarEventEditSheet.swift:415`); macOS has none. Scoped out of the first pass; file it separately if the owner wants Apple's edits to win. RC-TRIAGE: POST-RC, a deliberate feature change. **ADDENDUM 2026-10-29 (agent `onenote1250`) -- IMPLEMENTED.** The event editor draws ONE `Notes` field on both platforms and it is the rich Cadence `Note`. **What is new:** `Cadence/Shared/CadenceEventNotesMerge.swift` holds rules (1), (2), (4) and (6) as pure functions -- `shouldMirror`, `flattenedForCalendar`/`mirrorText`, `displayText`, `mergedContent`, `isEdit` -- so neither surface spells a decision of its own; `Cadence/Shared/Components/CadenceEventNotesField.swift` is the field's chrome (the label, the quiet read-only sentence, the failure notice, the Open control), with each platform passing in its own markdown editor -- `iOSMarkdownEditingSurface` and `MarkdownEditor` are one control's UIKit and AppKit implementations, which is the only difference between the two surfaces and is the one [[T-8201]] allows; `MacEventNoteCommit` (in `EventNoteSupportViews`) is `iOSEventNoteCommit`'s twin, so the Mac's two event-note editors share one ordered commit; `CadenceEventNoteSupport.canMirrorNotes(to:)` is rule (5). Retired: iOS `eventNoteSection` + `notesSection`, macOS `linkedNoteCard` + `CadenceSchedulePanelNotesRow(notes: $draft.notes)`, and [[T-422]]'s `allowsImageInsertion: false` -- the field writes `Note.content`, which `CadenceMarkdownSourceInventory` reads, so the image door closes on nothing (`theCalendarEventEditorRefusesImageInsertion` is replaced by `theCalendarEventEditorAcceptsImagesBecauseItsNotesFieldIsANoteRow`). **RULE (1), the anti-clobber rule, is a baseline per host**: the note's content as the editor opened it, advanced ONLY when Apple Calendar accepted a mirror, so a refused mirror retries and an untouched note never writes. Five commit paths ask it: the iOS field (`commitNotes`), the iOS note sheet (`persistNote` -- Done and a swipe-dismiss both commit with nothing typed), the Mac popover (`commitNotes`), the Mac note sheet (`commitEventNote`), and the one that was easiest to miss -- the iOS sheet's **Save**, which writes `EKEvent.notes` through `updateEvent` rather than through any note commit, and used to write back the notes the sheet opened with; `savedEventNotes` now returns the event's own notes unless the note moved. **RULE (6), the migration, is both shown and stored.** `mergedContent` appends the Apple text under a `---` divider and answers `nil` only when the two sides already agree (Apple empty, equal to the FLATTENED note, or already inside it) -- containment is what makes it idempotent, and comparing against the flattened note is why a note carrying a picture does not migrate against its own mirror. It is applied in `displayText`, so the field shows both halves, AND written into the note by `ensureEventNote` before the note reaches a keystroke or the full editor, because the full editor does not merge and its next commit would otherwise push the Cadence half over Apple's. Deliberately NOT written on open: nothing on `Note` records that a migration happened, so an open-time append would repeat on a read-only calendar for ever ([[T-8162]]). Both hosts write the body through `CadenceCoreNoteSupport.applyContent`, never a bare `note.content =`, which is what keeps the title and inline `#tags` in sync (`CadenceNoteTitleSyncSurfaceTests`). The Mac's field buffers typing and flushes on [[T-7810]]'s schedule: a `MarkdownEditor` writes its binding on every keystroke and this field's write reaches SwiftData *and* EventKit. **Mutation: 9/9 KILLED** over a scratch tree (baseline green, 22 tests) -- M1 `shouldMirror` always true; M2/M3 the iOS field's and Save's gates removed; M4 the migration refusing exactly when it is needed; M5 Apple's text replacing the note instead of being appended; M6 the containment guard removed (idempotence); M7 the migration shown but not stored; M8 `displayText` dropping the merge; M9 the mirror handing over raw source with its image references. **Seen on screen (iPad Pro 11, `calendar-cascade` fixture, EventKit disarmed, no real `EKEventStore` opened):** one `NOTES` field with the markdown toolbar and its image button; an event with no Cadence note showing its `EKEvent.notes` text (rule 4); after replacing that text, re-opening the event shows `Agenda: Q4 plan` over a rule over `Moved to the room on the fourth floor.` (rule 6); and the full Event Note editor, reached from Open, holding that same merged body -- which is the stored note, not the display. **NOT seen:** macOS, because `run-macos-app.sh` refuses while the owner's own Cadence is running ([[T-3259]]); and rule (5)'s quiet sentence, because `EKCalendar.allowsContentModifications` cannot be made false on a fixture calendar and a real read-only calendar needs a real store. Both are pinned by tests instead (`aReadOnlyCalendarSkipsTheMirrorRatherThanFailingIt`, `bothPlatformsDrawTheOneSharedNotesField`). Rule (7) is unchanged and pinned (`theMirrorIsSavedForThisOccurrenceOnBothPlatforms`). Tests: `CadenceTests/CadenceEventNotesMergeTests.swift` (22). **Part of this change landed early in `ad37ff2c`**: agent `ledgercard1230` swept 27 insertions into `CadenceTests/CadenceCodexFunctionalParityTests.swift`, including this ticket's `mirrorsToCalendar: isEditable` assertions, and chose not to revert them; they are correct where they are and are NOT in this commit. Residuals filed: [[T-8162]], [[T-8163]], [[T-8164]].
- [T-8162] **OPEN 2026-10-29 (agent `onenote1250`, from [[T-8160]]'s range, the commit carrying this line; found while implementing [[T-8161]] and deliberately not fixed there) -- [[T-8161]]'s migration is idempotent by CONTAINMENT, not by a marker, so on a READ-ONLY calendar a user who deletes the appended Apple Calendar paragraph gets it back on the next open, for ever.** The merge asks one question -- is Apple's text already inside the flattened note? On a writable calendar that settles after one mirror: the note is written back to `EKEvent.notes`, the two sides agree, and a later deletion mirrors too. On a read-only calendar nothing can ever be written to Apple Calendar, so the question is asked against text Cadence cannot change and the answer flips back to "no" the moment the user removes the paragraph. It is lossless and visible rather than silent, which is why it was accepted: the owner's rule is that Apple's text is never discarded, and re-showing text that genuinely still exists in Apple Calendar is arguably right. The durable fix is a marker saying "this note has taken that text once", and there is nowhere to put one -- `Note` has no spare field, a new one is a `CadenceSchema` change with CloudKit migration, and a device-local `UserDefaults` marker would let a second device re-append. Reproduce: a read-only event with both a Cadence note and different `EKEvent.notes`, delete the appended half, reopen.
- [T-8163] **OPEN 2026-10-29 (agent `onenote1250`, from [[T-8160]]'s range, the commit carrying this line; [[T-8161]] deferred this deliberately and said to file it separately) -- nothing re-reads `EKEvent.notes` after the Cadence note exists, so an Apple-side edit SURVIVES but never WINS.** [[T-8161]] rule (1) stops the clobber: an untouched Cadence note is never mirrored, so an edit made in Apple Calendar stays there, and rule (6) folds it into the field the next time it is drawn. What is still missing is the other direction -- an Apple edit made AFTER a Cadence edit is merged in under a divider rather than recognised as the newer text of the same paragraph, because nothing compares the two by time. iOS has a partial precedent in `iOSCalendarEventNoteReload.reloadedNotes` ([[T-5171]]), which refreshes a draft the user has not touched on every `EKEventStoreChanged`; macOS has none. This is a design question for the owner before it is a code one: it needs a rule for which side wins, and the only lossless answer available today is the divider the migration already uses.

The question to answer is whether a compact field inside an event sheet should mint tasks at all -- if yes, drop the flag; if no, say so on the field and consider whether the full editor should match.

- [T-7120] **CLOSED 2026-10-26 (agent `widgetfix2030`, the commit carrying this line; SEEN ON SCREEN FIXED on BOTH standing simulators -- `Cadence-iPhone15` and `Cadence-iPadPro11`, widget gallery, populated AND empty) -- THE CALENDAR WIDGET'S TWO-DIGIT DAY NUMBERS ARE LEGIBLE AT `systemSmall` AND `systemLarge`.** [[T-7121]] and [[T-7122]] close with it on one shared root cause. `widgetstates1800`'s diagnosis (`CadenceWidgets/CalendarSnapshotWidget.swift`, the day number at `.lineLimit(1).minimumScaleFactor(0.6)` in a cell too narrow for two glyphs) was reproduced first and is right, but the cell was narrower than that file's own arithmetic accounts for: **WidgetKit's default content margins were never disabled.** They are ~16pt a side, `scale.outerPadding` (12-16pt) is drawn INSIDE them, and together they spend 56pt of a 158pt `systemSmall` tile before the first cell is laid out -- three cells of ~31pt, ~13pt of glyph room, under the ~15pt `26` needs even at the minimum scale factor, so SwiftUI truncated instead of shrinking further. That is exactly why `1`-`8` (12pt) rendered and `10`+ did not, and why `SAT` became `S...` and `clear` became `cl...` in the same cells; the same 32pt came off the HEIGHT of the two medium tiles, which is [[T-7121]] and [[T-7122]]. Four changes here: `.contentMarginsDisabled()` on BOTH widget configurations (the views' own padding IS the margin); the cell's side inset split out of `.padding()` and cut to 6pt, or 5pt where seven columns share a 338pt tile; the `+ 1` dropped from the grid's day-number size, since the grid is the NARROWEST cell and was the one place the number was drawn LARGER; and the grid's column spacing 6 -> 4, which six gaps turn into 12pt of glyph width. Fixed in the same cell and also seen, not inferred: the long `due`/`planned` chip labels were truncating to `1 du` / `3 pl` on the iPad at `systemLarge` AND `systemExtraLarge` -- no family's day cell has the ~49pt `2 planned` needs -- so the strip says `d`/`p` at every family rather than spelling a word it cannot fit. AFTER, both devices, gallery: `MON 26 TUE 27 WED 28` at small and all fourteen of `26`-`31`, `1`-`8` at large, every weekday label and every `clear` caption whole. Scoped macOS run of the seven widget suites XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0, 1292 compile tasks, 0 warnings; iOS leg COMPILED, 655 app-target tasks, 0 warnings. The fallback task is cancelled and re-armed on every keystroke (`NoteEditorPane.swift:390-401`), so it is a pure debounce: a kill loses everything typed since the last 15 s pause or focus change -- unbounded during continuous typing. App deactivation does not move first responder, so switching away does not flush either; a kill with the user idle more than 15 s loses nothing. `CadenceAppDelegate.applicationWillTerminate` (`Cadence/macOS/Services/CadenceAppDelegate.swift:18`) banks the focus stopwatch and settles pending ticks but flushes no editor, and a purge kill runs no hook at all, so no terminate-side flush can cover this ticket's case -- only a shorter or capped window can. `NoteEditorPane.titleBinding` writes `note.title` per keystroke without committing (T-4971), so the title rides autosave latency. That holds for an untouched canvas but not for the very next gesture after a move: `editingTaskID` is set by `onLift` and is cleared only by a tap (canvas, all-day chip, timed event, the block's own inspector tap) or a new draft press -- nothing on the scroll path puts a block down (no `onScrollPhaseChange` in the file) -- so after a long-press move the block stays lifted, and the owner's natural next move is a swipe. The runner is explicitly built to refuse rather than guess -- `scripts/mutate.sh:192` ("nothing here silently regresses to the old wrong answer, it degrades to refusing to guess") and `:1631` ("naming a test that did not run, and must still refuse rather than borrow its result"). **So no past mutation verdict was silently wrong because of this**; an agent that hit it got a refusal and, like `partialcal`, dropped the optional field and re-ran. The verdict still names whatever goes red. **The cost is the lost check**, not a wrong result: without `tests:` nothing asserts that the test the mutation was aimed at is the test that caught it. **The size, measured:** `rg '@Test\("'` over `CadenceTests/` finds **263** occurrences in **22** files, against **5,758** plain `@Test func` -- about 4%. **The fix** is to match the display name as well as the function spelling, the same widening [[T-3212]] already did once for argument lists, and `mutate.sh selftest` is where it gets pinned. So the `Illegal attempt to establish a relationship between objects in different contexts` reading — argued from documented Core Data behaviour and never observed — **does not reproduce in SwiftData over this schema in this harness**, and the entry no longer claims it does. What it DOES do is worse than the bare-task case and is the reason the fix still matters: with no relationships the successor was at least saved through the retired context, whereas WITH them the successor **never reached the store at all** (the audit fetch for `recurrenceSpawnedTaskID` found nothing, `TaskCompletionAnimationManagerTests.swift:303`) and the parent's completion was lost with it (`:300`) — a recurring series silently stops. The mechanism is INFERRED, not measured: assigning the live relationships pulls the successor into the live context through the inverse side, exactly as this repo's own comment on `spawnNextOccurrenceIfNeeded` warns, so the retired context's `insert` and `save` had nothing of it to write. Both Latin pins hold UNCHANGED (`"Café--Plan!! 2026"` → `"cafe plan 2026"` and `normalize("!!!") == ""`). One existing expectation did change and it is the behaviour change, not a weakened assertion: `CadenceCodexSearchOptimizationTests.codexPreparedQueryPreservesScoresIncludingEmptyAndPunctuation` is a PARITY table (the `PreparedQuery` and `String` overloads agree), and its `("!!!", [], 1)` row became `("!!!", [], nil)`; three non-Latin rows were added to the same table. What it could not establish is the delay. The widget extension holds no mirroring delegate and `CadenceWidgets/CadenceWidgets.entitlements` carries no `icloud-container-identifiers`, so it cannot run an export for itself; the export therefore waits for the app. A task completed from a widget button by someone who rarely opens the app is the shape that bites. **Three options, and the choice is the owner's.** (1) **Leave it.** A widget completion syncs when Cadence is next opened; on a device where the widget *is* how the app is used, that could be days. (2) **Give the extension its own iCloud entitlement** so it mirrors for itself — a change to a signing input, and [[T-1309]] is this repository's record of what an unmeasured signing-input change costs. (3) **Stop writing from the extension**, routing the intents through the app instead, which costs the background completion the widget button exists for. **Nothing cheap closes it from here, and that was checked rather than assumed.** The app already posts the external-write marker (`CadenceStoreSupport.postExternalWrite`) and adopts it ([[T-306]], [[T-312]]), but adoption is about the app's own in-memory state, not about provoking an export — and there is no public API to start a mirroring pass, which is the same fact that makes a "Sync Now" button unbuildable ([[T-2000]]). **One theoretical loss path is left and is not exercised by anything in this tree:** a history purge that ran ahead of the mirroring delegate's token would drop an unexported transaction, and nothing in Cadence purges persistent history — there is no `NSPersistentHistoryChangeRequest` anywhere in the repository. **What would settle it: a two-device run.** Write from a widget on device A with the app not running, then watch device B — the same measurement [[T-2010]] and [[T-3046]] both stop at. Filed text: OPEN 2026-10-21 (filed by agent `k1ios` out of [[T-3160]], SEEN ON SCREEN on `Cadence-iPadPro11` and read in the source; NOT fixed because `Cadence/iOS/iOSCalendarView.swift` is in the Codex lease) -- on iOS a `cadence://calendar` link that arrives while Month is the view mode puts the day's own WEEK at the top of the grid, so on any day after about the 14th the header names the NEXT month and the agenda beside it reads "Nothing this month".** Seen 2026-10-21: Month opened through `cadence://calendar` showed "Nov 2026" over rows starting Oct 18, with October's days drawn as the dimmed out-of-month days and the agenda empty. Cause: `applyCalendarDeepLinkDate()` sets `anchorDate = day`, and `CadenceCalendarDateMemory.restoredPosition` returns `anchorDate: linked` on the cold path, while Month's anchor is meant to be `CadenceCalendarMonthWindow.topRow(forMonthContaining:)`, which `setViewMode` already uses; `displayedMonth` then reads the middle of a window that starts on today's week. Reachable from the Calendar widget's link. Fix: when the mode is Month, anchor a linked day on `topRow(forMonthContaining: day)` on both paths, and pin it with a pure test on the shared side. Not checked: the same path in Week mode opens a week starting on the linked day (Wed-Tue), which may be intended for the widget's fortnight; the macOS month page was not looked at.
- [T-3325] **OPEN 2026-10-21, RECHECKED 2026-10-25 STILL BLOCKED by agent `winctl1941` (the commit carrying this line): Claude Code's simulator tools refused `screenshot` and `attach` on `Cadence-iPadPro11` with "require an attended session", so the alerts were not looked at, no deep link was sent and nothing was seen; the other agent's success today was presumably an attended session. Claude Code's simulator tools refuse with "require an attended session", `simctl` has no tap, and the host Simulator app is off limits, so nothing here can press Cancel/Open. To do, in an ATTENDED session: tap Cancel on both alerts (or Open, which delivers the link), then launch the build with a private store (`simulator-claim.sh claim <id> 1800 ipad`, `-CadenceSuiteName <id> -ios.calendar.viewMode Month`), send `cadence://calendar`, tap Open, and confirm the header reads the linked day's month ("Oct 2026" on 21 Oct) and the agenda is not "Nothing this month"; also once with `cadence://calendar/2026-10-31`. Note for every agent: `simctl openurl` on this Xcode raises the confirmation alert every time, so it cannot drive a deep link unattended.

- [T-3311] **CLOSED 2026-10-22 (agent `decvis`, the commit carrying this line; filed 2026-10-21 by agent `k1ios` out of [[T-3160]], SEEN ON SCREEN on `Cadence-iPadPro11` portrait) -- the iPad month grid's EVENT chip draws its calendar glyph on the TIME LINE, so the title row is the title's. Seen again on `Cadence-iPadPro11` at 11-inch portrait through the [[T-3186]] `calendar-hues` fixture: the three timed chips in the Oct 22 cell now read "Deep re...", "Pure bl..." and "Pale ev..." where they read "Dee...", "Pure..." and "Pale...", with the `calendar.badge.clock` sitting beside `9:15a` / `10:15a` / `11:30a` on the row below.** Not a paint or contrast fault: the colours are right (see [[T-3160]]). Options: drop the glyph below a cell width, let the time line carry the glyph, or give the grid more width in portrait. **OWNER DECISION 2026-10-22 (recorded by the coordinator from the owner's answers in session; no code written yet): MOVE THE CALENDAR GLYPH ONTO THE CHIP'S TIME LINE, freeing the title row. Not the drop-below-a-width option and not a wider portrait grid: the glyph's information is kept, the title gets the cell.** **Fix.** `CadenceCalendarChipGlyphRow.forChip(hasTimeLine:)` (`Cadence/Shared/CadenceCalendarMonthCellPriority.swift`) is the rule and `iOSCalendarMiniChip` reads it for BOTH rows, so the glyph cannot be drawn twice or dropped. It is stated as a function of "is there a time line" rather than of "is this an event": a chip with no time line has nowhere to move its glyph to, so the task chip in the same grid and the all-day chip in the iOS strip keep theirs on the title row, which is why the all-day "Dee..." in the sighting is unchanged. The rule lives in Shared because `iOSCalendarMiniChip` is inside `#if os(iOS)` and the suite that witnesses it runs on the macOS leg. macOS needs nothing: `MonthEventChip` draws no glyph at all. Held by `CadenceCalendarChipTreatmentTests.theMonthChipsGlyphMovesToItsTimeLineAndLeavesTheTitleTheCell`.
- [T-3198] **CLOSED 2026-10-22 (agent `tool2137`, the commit carrying this line; TOOLING, all three named defects handled) -- `scripts/mutate.sh` now refuses a bad plan in its PREFLIGHT, before any lease or baseline, and `--check` runs that preflight alone; `CadenceSourceScan.codeOnly`'s doc says it blanks string literals.** **The preflight** (`preflight()`, pure, called from `run_plan` once the baselines are read and before the test-host lock): **(1)** every hunk's needle is counted against the bytes the run will mutate, simulated hunk by hunk as `apply_mutation` applies them, and a count other than the plan's `count:` refuses `NEEDLE-AMBIGUOUS` (lines named, "check its leading whitespace against every site") or `NEEDLE-ABSENT` up front, where both used to wait for the baseline queue; **(2)** a `suite:` containing `/` refuses `SUITE-PREFIXED` (the runner prepends `CadenceTests/` itself, which is what died in `shutil.copyfile`), and a suite the tree's own `scripts/test-suite-index.sh` does not list refuses `UNKNOWN-SUITE`; **plus one the entry did not name and [[T-3341]] proved was the real cost:** a `tests:` name the suite does not declare refuses `TEST-NOT-IN-SUITE` and NAMES THE SUITE THAT DOES. If the index cannot be read (the `wait-mutate.sh selftest` stub tree's exits 1), the suite and `tests:` checks are skipped and the run says so; the needle check still runs. A refusal exits 2 and removes the pid marker, since nothing was edited. **(3)** `codeOnly`'s doc now says a needle that is a literal's content (an `icon:` SF Symbol, a copy string) cannot be found in that form, and points at `strippingComments(_:)`. **Real-subject proof:** `--check` over a three-mutation plan on `CadenceSchedulePanel.swift` (W1 the [[T-3169]] mis-scope, W2 `suite: CadenceTests/...`, W3 `count: 2` over a 1-site needle) exits 2 with `TEST-NOT-IN-SUITE ... it is declared in CadenceTodayTimelineDraftCreationTests`, `SUITE-PREFIXED` and `NEEDLE-AMBIGUOUS ... (lines 797)`; the correctly scoped plan exits 0. Index: 579 suites, 6366 tests. **Selftest:** a new T-3198 block, 11 checks, 106/106 in the full file; `wait-mutate.sh selftest` 11/11. `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests.mutationRunnerRefusals` gains `SUITE-PREFIXED`, `UNKNOWN-SUITE`, `TEST-NOT-IN-SUITE`, so deleting one from the body or the selftest reddens it. **Mutation-tested 6/6 KILLED on a `git archive` scratch copy of `scripts/`, never the shared tree**, each mutant run to completion and the copy restored byte-identical: the `/` check disabled (1 red, it falls through to UNKNOWN-SUITE), the count comparison disabled (1 red), `TEST-NOT-IN-SUITE` disabled (3 red), the in-order hunk simulation disabled (1 red), `_ran`'s label needle without its closing quote (1 red), and the `run_plan` wiring cut (`problems = []`: the W-plan `--check` exits 0 instead of 2). XCODEBUILD evidence in the commit message. [[T-3182]] [[T-3190]] [[T-3191]] [[T-3341]]
  - **Filed as:** **OPEN 2026-10-16 (filed by the coordinator from three defects one agent hit in a single session; TOOLING, every one caught before it produced false evidence, none touched product code) -- a mutation plan and a source-scan assertion both fail LATE and confusingly, after a lease is taken and a baseline is built, when a cheap up-front check would refuse them in a second.** All three came from agent `compactcascade` while verifying [[T-3184]] and [[T-3185]]; it caught all three itself, which is the only reason none of them became a wrong verdict. **(1) An indentation-sensitive needle matched 2 of 3 sites.** The plan's `view-stops-z-ordering` needle carried leading whitespace, so it silently matched a subset. A mutation that mutates fewer sites than intended still reports `KILLED` and still looks like evidence. Caught before any mutation was applied; the runner was stopped, restored cleanly (`status=143`) and relaunched. **(2) `mutate.sh`'s `suite:` takes a BARE suite name and prepends `CadenceTests/` itself.** Passing the already-prefixed `CadenceTests/CadenceCalendarOverlapLayoutTests` produced a double prefix, hence a log path containing a slash, which blew up inside `shutil.copyfile` **during the baseline**. It failed safely -- the tree check reported `OK` on all four mutated files, so nothing was stranded -- but the message was a Python stdlib error, not a refusal naming the real mistake, and the cost was a full relaunch after a long queue wait. **(3) `CadenceSourceScan.codeOnly` blanks STRING LITERALS as well as comments.** An assertion searching a chip for its `icon:` literal therefore searched an erased string and failed -- **a test that goes red on a change that landed correctly**, which is the most expensive kind of false signal because the obvious response is to "fix" working code. This trap is already documented once in the tree (`CadenceCalendarChipTreatmentTests` notes that reading through `codeOnly` makes an SF-Symbol assertion pass vacuously) and it has now bitten twice. **What would end all three cheaply: a `mutate.sh --check <plan>` that runs before any lease or baseline** and refuses with a named reason when a needle matches zero or an unexpected number of sites, when a `suite:` value already carries the `CadenceTests/` prefix, or when a suite name does not resolve -- the same shape as `xcb.sh`'s existing `UNKNOWN-SUITE` refusal, which exists for exactly this reason on the other side of the house. For (3), the durable fix is a doc line on `codeOnly` itself stating that string literals are blanked and pointing at `strippingComments`, since the knowledge currently lives in one test's comment where only its next reader finds it. - [T-3212] **CLOSED 2026-10-18 (agent `mutateparam`, Batch C, the commit carrying this line; MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER ON THE REAL SUBJECT and MUTATION-PROVEN) -- `scripts/mutate.sh` now reads a parameterised `@Test(arguments:)` test at both ends: it is seen to RUN and its failure is ATTRIBUTED.** One shared pattern, `ARG_LIST = \((?:[A-Za-z0-9_]+:)*\)`, now follows the function name in all three places that required a literal `()`: `classify_run`'s `_ran` (now `re.search("Test " + re.escape(t) + ARG_LIST)`), the failure harvest `FAILED_SWIFT_TESTING`, and the result count `TEST_RESULT` -- the third was an unfiled part of the same defect: a parameterised test's `with 4 test cases passed` line was not counted, so a suite of only parameterised tests would have read NO-TESTS-RAN. The `(` must follow the name immediately, so a plan naming a PREFIX of a test that ran still refuses TEST-ABSENT. **Real subject, `CalendarBoardDayDropCommitTests.mobileDayDropRestoresEveryMutatedFieldOnlyWhenRefused` (Codex-leased test file READ, not edited; product code mutated in a scratch tree only):** naming it in `tests:`, the old runner refused `BASELINE-NOT-GREEN / TEST-ABSENT` over a baseline `green over 12 tests`; the new one baselines `green over 13 tests` and runs. Mutation Q1 (`CadenceTaskMutationSupport.moveTaskToDate` materialises 31, not 30): old runner `INVALID (RED-WITHOUT-A-FAILING-TEST)` with 2 `recorded an issue with 2 arguments` lines in the log; new runner `KILLED -- killed by: mobileDayDropRestoresEveryMutatedFieldOnlyWhenRefused`. Q2 (`<= 0` to `< 0`) the same. A THIRD shape the ticket did not name, measured on mutation P1 (`moveTaskToDate` returns `true`): when a plain test ALSO failed, the old runner printed `KILLED` naming only that one and silently dropped the parameterised killer; the new one names both. All three mutations applied, compiled (0 errors) and were restored byte-identical. **Selftest:** a new `T-3212` block in `mutate.sh selftest` built from that real run's own lines (zero-width-space prefixes, `Test case passing 2 arguments` progress lines, `with 4 test cases failed`) -- one fixture that must be SURVIVED green with the test named, KILLED red and attributed by function name, `(_:)` read the same, and prefix names refused; 93/93. Each of the four edits reverted on a scratch copy turns it red (2, 3, 2 and 6 checks). The [[T-786]] label map still covers a display-named parameterised test (`@Test("...", arguments:)` logs the quoted label; `test-suite-index.sh --test-labels` maps `anotherKeyIsNotThePanelsToTake` and `escapeUnderACommandFamilyModifierIsLeftAlone`), pinned by a check. Also fixed: selftest's `check()` raised `TypeError` on a non-string `detail` on exactly the failing path, aborting the report of every later check; it now `str()`s it. Not changed: `tests:` still takes the BARE function name -- `foo(refuses:estimate:)` there still reads TEST-ABSENT, which is the documented spelling, not a defect. Filed as: **OPEN 2026-10-17 (filed by agent `blocktail` when `scripts/mutate.sh` refused its own plan; TOOLING, and the refusal was CORRECT -- this is a false negative that blocks evidence, never one that fakes it) -- `mutate.sh` cannot mutation-test a parameterised `@Test(arguments:)` test, because its ran-check needles a spelling swift-testing never prints for one.** `classify_run`'s `_ran(t)` asks `("Test %s()" % t) in log` -- the function name followed by an EMPTY argument list. A parameterised case logs as `Test mobileDayDropRestoresEveryMutatedFieldOnlyWhenRefused(refuses:estimate:)`, so the needle cannot match, and the whole batch refuses `BASELINE-NOT-GREEN / TEST-ABSENT` over a baseline that was in fact green. **No spelling in the plan's `tests:` line fixes it from the caller's side**: naming the labels yields `...(refuses:estimate:)()`, which matches nothing either. The [[T-786]] label map is the nearest existing machinery and does not cover this -- it maps a function name to a `@Test("display name")` string, which is a different thing from argument labels. **Measured population: 5 `@Test(arguments:)` sites in `CadenceTests/`**, four of them in Codex-leased `CadenceCodex*` files, so most of the affected tests cannot be worked around by de-parameterising them either. **Why it matters more than 5 suggests:** parameterised tests are exactly the ones that assert a behaviour across BOTH answers -- refused and taken, true and false -- which is the shape a mutation most needs as its control. [[T-3170]]'s shared-helper pass hit this trying to prove that `moveTaskToDate` no longer writes block-membership fields in EITHER answer. **Not a correctness hazard.** The guard fails closed: it refuses rather than printing a verdict it has not earned, which is the whole design of that runner ([[T-530]], [[T-1245]]). The cost is that the evidence cannot be collected at all, and an agent who does not read the refusal carefully will conclude its suite is red. **Next action:** teach `_ran` the parameterised spelling -- match `Test <name>(` with any argument list, not `Test <name>()` -- and add a selftest fixture for it, since `mutate.sh selftest` currently has no parameterised case and that absence is why this shipped. Verify against a real parameterised subject, not a synthetic one.

  **The manager half, which the ticket asked for.** `iOSCalendarManager.fetchEvents(for:)` now consults `CadenceCalendarFixtureEvents.timedEvents(for:)` **and** `.allDayEvents(for:)` AHEAD of the authorization guard and returns their whole answer, sorted by the shared `CadenceCalendarEventSearchSupport.precedes`. NOT SEEN ON SCREEN. **STILL TO DO:** (a) the drag-a-task-onto-a-task gesture (`insertBundle(from:adding:)`) on the Mac timeline (`TimelineTaskBlock` / `TimelineDayCanvas.formBundle`), the iOS day timeline (`iOSCalendarTimelineViews.formBundle`) and the iOS board (`iOSCalendarBoardView`, Codex-leased) — best removed together so the cross-platform parity pins in `CadenceBundleCreationParityTests` go in one step; (b) every surface that shows or edits an existing block (timeline/board block views, block detail sheets and inspectors, Focus block mode, month/agenda chips, search, widgets — much of it in the leased paths listed in the first pass); (c) the archive import unbundling on the way in (draft still held at `scratchpad/debundle/`). **Earlier passes —** **PARTIAL 2026-10-14 (agent `debundle`) — the one-time migration that takes the Block feature's rows out of the store WITHOUT taking its members' time with them is written, tested and landed; the removal passes that follow it have not started.** The hazard this ticket was filed over is closed: `Cadence/Services/CadenceTaskBundleRetirement.swift` is a new startup pass that, for every `TaskBundle` in the store, pushes the block's day and time down onto its members in `bundleOrder` order, detaches them and deletes the block — so no member is left holding the `-1` unscheduled sentinel `assignTask` wrote on it. **The layout, decided and stated rather than discovered:** members whose natural lengths (`max(estimatedMinutes, 5)`) fit the block's duration are laid end to end from `bundle.startMin`; members that do NOT fit share the block's own span in equal integer slices (`span * index / count`) so that nobody spills past the block's end onto a part of the day the user never gave it — they overlap instead, which `CadenceCalendarOverlapLayout` already draws and which is the honest rendering of a block that was always overcommitted. More members than minutes collapses some slices, so those members share a start and their relative order falls to the overlap solver's tie-break; that is the one ordering promise the pass does not make, and it says so. **No member's `estimatedMinutes` is rewritten** — an estimate is user data that Focus, planning totals and an hours-mode `Goal` read; a migration may move a start, it may not invent a duration. A block with **zero members** has nothing to push down and is simply deleted. Creating and editing differ by whether the record exists and by that one button — not by being different screens. **Two picker rulings from the owner, and one of them is new work:** the date selector must be **Cadence's own** — `Cadence/Shared/Components/CadenceDatePicker.swift` already exists and is the grid to use, NOT a system `DatePicker`. The time selector must be **a roller that rolls hour and minute SEPARATELY**, and **nothing like it exists in the tree**: a sweep for `WheelDatePickerStyle`, `.wheel` and hour/minute pickers returns nothing, and `Cadence/Shared/Components/CadenceStartTimeFieldRow.swift` takes a flat `@Binding var minutes: Int`. One panel means the next change to what a task HAS is one edit. **Sequencing:** [[T-3169]] is building the iPad create panel now and is the first instance of this shape — it should be written as the shared panel from the start rather than retrofitted, and this ticket then adopts it at the other seven sites. - [T-3074] **CLOSED 2026-10-09 by the OWNER, and it was never a code defect — the fix was two taps in Settings.** The owner reports Today's sun is amber again. Diagnosis confirmed by agent `sidebarspacing` and acted on by the owner: a `today:<hex>` pair was sitting in `CadencePreferenceKeys.sidebarTabColors`, which the Mac's Settings → Sidebar picker writes and `CadenceLookPreferenceSync` syncs, so it was overriding `CadenceFeatureDestination.defaultColorHex`'s `Theme.amberHex` on every surface at once. **Nothing was hardcoded to yellow**, deliberately: that would have broken the picker for all nine destinations to fix one stored value. Reset was reachable because [[T-245]] made `CadenceColorPalette.destinationTints` exactly `Theme`'s own six accents, precisely so a default could never become unreachable — that decision is what made this a two-tap fix rather than a code change. **The one real gap this surfaced stays open and is NOT this ticket:** iOS has no tint editor at all (`iOSSidebarLayoutSettingsSection` reorders and hides, and only *reads* the tint), so an owner with no Mac could not have undone this. Whether iOS grows a tint editor or a plain Reset to default is a product question nobody has asked for yet. **OPEN 2026-10-08 (filed by agent `sidebarspacing`, owner action, NOT a code defect) — Today's sun is purple because a stored sidebar-tint override says so; the default is already amber and nothing in the tree hardcodes a hue.** The owner: *"for today's icon, it was a yellow sun but now it's a purple sun. change it back to yellow on all platforms."* Established before touching anything, because the two possible causes have opposite fixes. `CadenceFeatureDestination.defaultColorHex` returns `Theme.amberHex` for `.today`, and every surface resolves through it: macOS's `SidebarStaticDestination.resolvedColorHex(from:)`, `CadenceSidebarTint.hex(for:overridesRaw:)` for the iPad column, `iOSTasksTabView` and `iOSSearchView` — a tree-wide read of `Theme.purple`/`purpleHex` finds no `.today` site at all, and amber is a warm orange in all three palettes. So a `<destination>:<hex>` pair for `today` is sitting in `CadencePreferenceKeys.sidebarTabColors`, which macOS's Settings → Sidebar colour picker writes and `CadenceLookPreferenceSync` syncs to every device. The rolled-back-on-throw path in `CadenceSavedLinkPersistence.delete` is failure handling, not user undo: a *successful* delete is final. Pin it in `CadenceTests/CadenceSavedLinkPersistenceTests.swift` (NOT leased), which already source-scans both link surfaces: the mobile delete must be reachable only through the confirmation, and the confirmation copy must contain the link's title. **THE STYLING HALF IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE AND IS AN OWNER DECISION.** Codex's bullet mixed a destructive-action difference with a visual one — Mac draws shadowed `cadenceCard` rows, mobile draws plain ruled `List` rows. Mobile landed at `db2f214d` and the Mac half lands here, so all three vocabularies now have one owner and nothing in this entry is outstanding.  **Earlier:** **PARTIAL 2026-10-09 (agent `notesvocab`; filed by agent `noteslabels`; Codex parity audit, the "Notes labels/order" bullet; STOPPED on a width measurement rather than shipped, and the remainder is an owner decision) — the Mac's Notes vocabulary is ~44pt too wide for the phone's Notes header, so two of the four mobile labels are short ON PURPOSE; but the wide iPad reads the phone's abbreviations for no reason, and that half is a real defect.** Codex's premise is CONFIRMED on both halves, wording and order. **Mac** (`Cadence/macOS/Views/NotesView.swift:17-24`, `NotesPage.title`): `Daily` / `Weekly` / `Notepad` / `Event Notes`. **Mobile** (`Cadence/Shared/CadenceNotePlanningSupport.swift:70-77`, `CadenceMobileNotesTab.shortLabel`): `Daily` / `Weekly` / `Events` / `Pad`. **THE ORDER DIFFERS TOO, and Codex was right to print them in that order**: the Mac's `allCases` is `daily, weekly, notepad, meeting`, mobile's is `today, week, events, notepad` — so the notepad tab is THIRD on the Mac and FOURTH on mobile, and the event tab is fourth on the Mac and third on mobile. The last two tabs are transposed, not merely renamed. **WHY THIS STOPPED. The two short labels are a measured, deliberate, test-pinned decision, not an oversight.** `CadenceMobileNotesTab.shortLabelCharacterBudget = 6` with the comment *"Nothing here may exceed this, or the strip stops fitting beside the title on the narrowest supported phone"*; `CadenceNotePlanningSupport.swift:48-51` names the two exact strings — *"'Event Notes' and 'Notepad' are the two that do not fit beside the title on a 402pt phone, so they read 'Events' and 'Pad' here"*; and `iOSNotesTabMetrics.compactHorizontalPadding:1058-1064` records the in-situ measurement — the phone's inset was dropped from 12pt to 6pt and *"at 6 the row lands with about 12pt to spare"*. Three tests in `CadenceTests/MobileNotesAndSettingsShapeTests.swift` hold it: `everyShortLabelFitsBesideTheTitleOnOneRow` (the budget), `shortLabelsAreDistinct`, and `theTwoLongLabelsAreTheShortenedOnes`, whose own doc says *"this is the assertion that fails if someone 'restores' the long spellings and quietly reintroduces the clipping"*. The decision is commit `775833de` (2026-08-15, *"Two of twelve settings on screen, and a notes title that repeated the tab"*), which states the swap and why in its message. **It carries no T-id and is in NO ledger** — `ledger-view.sh brief` has nothing on the notes header or the short labels — so this is a recorded decision one notch weaker than a CLOSED ticket, which is exactly why it is being re-filed here rather than overridden in passing. **THE NUMBER.** Re-measured independently at 13pt semibold (system font, the strip's own size): `Daily` 31.4pt, `Weekly` 45.8pt, `Events` 42.4pt, `Pad` 23.9pt against `Notepad` 54.0pt and `Event Notes` 76.1pt. Through the strip's real geometry — `max(44, width + 2 × inset)` per tab, 2pt spacing — the short strip is **206.2pt** at the phone's 6pt inset and the Mac-vocabulary strip is **261.9pt**, a **+55.7pt** delta against the **~12pt** of slack the row actually has. The Mac's four words are about **44pt over budget on a 390pt phone**, and the header also holds a back control, the date title (`Aug 17–23` measures 77.2pt at 15pt bold) and the template button. `.fixedSize(horizontal: true)` on the strip (`iOSNotesView.swift:962`) means the overflow would not even truncate gracefully — it would push the row, and the file's own comment says *"a tab going to 'Eve…' costs the label its meaning"*. So the phone cannot have the Mac's words on this header as it is built. **WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IS NOT THE PHONE.** `iOSNotesHeader` renders `tab.shortLabel` unconditionally (`iOSNotesView.swift:947-955`) while already forking `isRegularWidth` one line below for the inset alone — so the iPad, whose narrowest Notes pane is 646pt (`docs/TODO.md:20`) against a 261.9pt long-label strip at the 12pt inset, shows `Pad` and `Events` with hundreds of points to spare. THAT is the half worth fixing and the half Codex's *"including wide iPad"* was pointing at. **Three options for the owner, in order of cost.** (1) **Regular width only**: add a full-length label beside `shortLabel` and read it when `horizontalSizeClass == .regular`, leaving the phone untouched. Cheapest, and it makes the iPad agree with the Mac word for word; the cost is that the phone and iPad then read differently, which the iOS guide's *"iPhone and iPad share one style; they differ by layout, not by row/chip/header vocabulary"* rule explicitly forbids — so this needs the owner to say the rule yields here. (2) **Everywhere, by buying the width back**: the Mac vocabulary fits the phone only if the header gives up ~44pt, which means moving the date title off the row or scrolling the strip — and the scrolling strip is the thing `775833de` removed. - [T-3088] **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (agent `monthpriority`, the commit carrying this line) — on an overfull month-grid day the calendar EVENTS take the chip slots and the TASKS overflow into "+N more", on both platforms, through one shared function.** **THE SURVEY FIRST, because the two platforms did not agree and the Mac was the one that was wrong.** macOS's `MonthDayCell` (`Cadence/macOS/Views/CalendarPageMonthSupportViews.swift`) derived a slot count from the row height it was given (`CalendarMonthCellLayout.chipLayout`) and then filled it `bundles.prefix(layout.visible)` -> `tasks.prefix(remaining)` -> `events.prefix(remaining)`: **events were LAST**, so a crowded day hid its events and kept its tasks, and it drew the task chips above the event chips to match. iOS's `iOSCalendarMonthDayCell` (`Cadence/iOS/iOSCalendarMonthViews.swift`) was already events-before-tasks, but through three hardcoded per-kind caps — `bundles.prefix(3)`, `events.prefix(max(0, 4 - bundles))`, `tasks.prefix(max(0, 5 - bundles - events))` — over a fixed five-slot cell rather than a measured one. So **one platform had the rule, neither stated it, and no line of either was reachable from the other**; the answer was insertion order on one side and three interlocking literals on the other. **THE OWNER'S REASONING, recorded on the type rather than here:** an event is a time-bound commitment you cannot reschedule unilaterally, so a hidden event costs the reader more than a hidden task, which can move without asking anybody; and it is the ranking Apple Calendar and Fantastical already trained the user on. **THE FIX** is `CadenceCalendarMonthCellPriority.split(bundles:events:tasks:capacity:)` in `Cadence/Shared/`, called by both cells and by nothing else. It returns a per-kind `Split` of counts rather than items, because macOS holds `CalendarEventItem`s and iOS holds `EKEvent`s and the ordering is a fact about the *kinds*. **Capacity stays each platform's own** and deliberately so: macOS's is derived from the row height (minus the slot the "+N more" label takes), the iPhone's is a fixed `chipCapacity = 5` because those rows have a `minHeight` and no budget to divide. How many rows there are is a layout question; who gets them is this one. **Bundles keep the rank both platforms already gave them** — a bundle is the shape of the day rather than one of its items, and the owner's argument ranks events against *tasks*. **TWO THINGS CHANGED BEYOND THE ORDERING, both stated rather than slipped in.** (1) macOS now draws its event chips ABOVE its task chips, so the surviving chips read top-down as what matters most and the two platforms draw the same order; pinned by `theMacMonthCellDrawsEventChipsAboveTaskChips`. (2) iOS loses its per-kind sub-caps, so a day with five events and no bundles now draws five event chips where it drew four and a task. That is the sub-caps being the drift rather than the rule: a second spelling of a priority is what the two cells had, and keeping one platform's arbitrary 3-and-4 would have meant the shared function taking per-platform parameters, which is the same drift wearing a parameter list. **The "+N more" count now comes off the same `Split` that produced the chips** (`split.hidden`, not a second subtraction), so the chips and the number above them cannot describe different days. **MUTATION-PROVEN.** `split`'s fill order reversed to tasks-before-events (the `drawnEvents`/`drawnTasks` pair swapped): it COMPILED, and was killed by `CalendarMonthCellPriorityTests.anOverfullMonthDayDrawsItsEventsAndOverflowsItsTasks` and `.whenEventsAloneOverflowTheCellNoTaskTakesASlotFromThem`. Restored byte-identical from a `cp` backup. **The test asserts the PARTITION, not the remainder**, which is the whole point: a day of three events and six tasks in four slots has a remainder of five under either ordering, so `#expect(hidden == 5)` alone is green for the behaviour this ticket was filed about. **Green:** macOS `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`, 0 warnings; iOS `generic/platform=iOS Simulator` `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`, 0 warnings.
```sh
# DEFECTIVE AS WRITTEN -- do not copy. `eventMessage CONTAINS` matches /usr/bin/log's own
# invocation records, both counters rise together, and this reads outstanding=0 over a standing
# prompt. Use `./scripts/xcb.sh check-automation` (T-2070, corrected 2026-10-07 by `envguard`).
req=$(/usr/bin/log show --last 6h --predicate 'process == "testmanagerd" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "Writer daemon requires authentication"' | grep -c 'Writer daemon requires')
don=$(/usr/bin/log show --last 6h --predicate 'process == "testmanagerd" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "Finished enabling Automation Mode"' | grep -c 'Finished enabling')
outstanding=$((req - don))   # >0 means a prompt is standing and NO macOS test run can work
```

Measured both ways on 2026-10-04: against the healthy host at 15:1x it reads `requests=1 finished=1 outstanding=0`, and against the wedged window (`--start '11:23:00' --end '14:00:00'`, cut before the 14:35:23 release) it reads `requests=1 finished=0 outstanding=1`. It costs **2.2s** and needs no privilege. Do NOT probe for the *"Enable UI Automation"* string alone — that line is still in the log long after the prompt is answered, so it reports a false positive on a healthy host; the pairing is the signal. If one is outstanding, `xcb.sh` should refuse with its own exit code and SAY the owner must authenticate — the same shape as the existing screen-lock refusal, which is the precedent for a preflight that reads host state and declines. **(b) Tell the 445s signature apart from a real failure.** A macOS run whose log reaches *"Received new test session connection"* but never *"requested serialized transport"*, and dies ~445s later with *"The test runner hung before establishing connection"*, is THIS, never a code defect — the zero-test guard currently reports it as an ordinary red and the mutation guard reads a zero-test run as a survivor, which is how a wedged host destroys evidence silently. Note the shell trap when writing the check: a shell function named `log` shadows the binary and makes `log show …` print *"too many arguments"*, so the preflight must call `/usr/bin/log` by absolute path. **Do not "fix" this by disabling automation mode or writing to the authorization database** — that is the line [[T-1742]] and [[T-2049]] already cost someone.
