- [T-626] **CLOSED 2026-09-18 (`e4719e3`) — iOS registers for the silent push CloudKit sync depends on, and the background mode reaches the built app.** The owner lifted this ticket's park themselves (*"i do use the ios one so do make sure to implement ios specific bugs"*), so the "BLOCKED ON iOS DISTRIBUTION" line below is expired and was still being read as current two days after the fix shipped ([[T-1298]]). **The rest of this entry is the analysis written before it landed, kept as filed; the commit message is where the reasoning for what shipped lives.** Originally: **iOS omits the background mode CloudKit silent-sync needs — latent, and BLOCKED ON iOS
  DISTRIBUTION. Do not implement this until that changes.** VERIFIED 2026-09-01 from CXT-016;
  all three source facts re-verified 2026-09-01 while closing [[T-652]].
  **The gate, plainly.** iOS is built but not distributed: `docs/apple-release-readiness.md` contains
  no occurrence of "iOS", "iPhone" or "iPad" — the two channels are the Mac App Store and Developer
  ID. So the impact on any shipping build today is **zero**, and the ticket's whole cost is a
  regression risk in the bundle that *does* ship.
  **The defect is broader than filed: iOS does not register either.** `CadenceAppDelegate` is
  `Cadence/macOS/Services/CadenceAppDelegate.swift`, installed by `@NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor`,
  and there is **no `UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor` anywhere in the repo**. It is the sole caller of
  `registerForRemoteNotifications()`, which
  `CadenceLaunchWiringTests.onlyTheRegistrarAsksAppKitToRegister` pins to that one file. On iOS,
  Cadence neither declares the capability nor registers for it.
  **Why it cannot be done by accident, and what to do when it can be done.** One app target, one
  `Cadence/Info.plist` (`INFOPLIST_FILE` names it in Debug and Release alike), so `UIBackgroundModes`
  added for iOS also ships in the **macOS** bundle — and the
  `#expect(info["UIBackgroundModes"] == nil)` it would break is a *deliberate* App Store
  review-hygiene check, not an oversight. That test
  (`AppStoreReviewReadinessTests.appInfoPlistContainsReviewReadyPrivacyKeys`) now **says so in its
  own doc comment**, including the instruction for the day iOS ships: satisfy the assertion's
  *intent* — "the macOS bundle declares no background mode" — by splitting the plist per platform or
  conditionalising the key, and re-point the `#expect`. Deleting the line removes the check rather
  than satisfying it.
  **The same change also closed the hole that made the guard bypassable.** `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE
  = YES`, so the shipped plist is that file merged with the target's `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` build
  settings — and ticking Background Modes in Xcode's capability editor writes
  `INFOPLIST_KEY_UIBackgroundModes` into `project.pbxproj` and never touches `Cadence/Info.plist`.
  The mode would have shipped with the `nil` assertion still green. The test now reads
  `project.pbxproj` too. Residue from that reading: [[T-665]].

The one net new finding is filed as [[T-1132]] instead.** The

    MarkdownTaskEmbedRenderInfo.untitledTaskTitle` is a constant), and the lookaround is required
    because `task.title == MarkdownTaskEmbedRenderInfo.untitledTaskTitle` is a **comparison** in the
    same file.
  - The index: same-file `func`s that report under the plain screen vocabulary, are not `body`,
    answer nothing a caller could guard on, and touch the store in no way at all — no insert, no
    delete, no commit and no swallowed commit. About 20+ helpers app-wide.

  readers — `reportOffenders` **and** `indirectReportOffenders` — but the `followingHandedOnReports`
  seam, and therefore the cost test, exists on the **first only**. So the test written to satisfy

  - `indirectReportOffenders` + arm: **6 more files**, unmeasured because nothing covers that

    - `iOSCalendarBoardView.handleDrop` — the `-> Bool` is `dropDestination`'s *"I consumed this

  *sideways* one frame down.** Found while landing [[T-636]](b), and it is the reason three of

  `NotePanel.toggleEmbeddedSubtask` / `renameEmbeddedTask` and the `ListNotesSupportViews` and

  the detector sees the iOS one and not the macOS three.

  **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-12 (agent `parkeddecisions`) against HEAD, with the arm implemented and
  swept rather than read.** Nothing below was inherited: since the 2026-09-06 figures, 33 commits
  have touched `Cadence/` — the tree the sweep reads — and 3 have touched

  - **The index is 269 helpers app-wide, not "about 20+".** That estimate was the figure furthest
    from the truth, and the width is the arm, not a detail of it.
  - **`reportOffenders`: 2 → 6.** Four additions, four files.
  - **`indirectReportOffenders`: 1 → 17.** Sixteen additions, seven files.
  - **Ten distinct files go red**, across two sweeps —
    `noSwallowedSaveIsFollowedByADismissOrACompletionHandler` and
    `noSuccessReportFollowsACommitSwallowedOneFrameDown`.

  **The triage, every addition by name rather than by count.**
  - **Real: 4 of 20.** `iOSCalendarSettingsSection.saveCalendarLinks` is unchanged since 2026-09-06

  `iOSFocusView.logBundleSession` calls `CadenceFocusSupport.logElapsedSeconds(_:across:)` →

  container's `loggedMinutes` with `+=` for every ticked member, then runs
  `try? modelContext.save()` and `resetTimer()`. Same defect and same fix as (c): the accumulators
  make *"the next fetch corrects it"* false, and the reset destroys the only copy of the seconds.
  **No half of the rule could see it**, which was the interesting part: nothing was inserted or
  deleted, and `resetTimer()` is not in half 2's success vocabulary. macOS's bundle timer commits
  through the same helper and belongs in the same pass.
  **[[T-621]] changed that half of the sentence (2026-09-03).** Banking a session inserts a
  `FocusSessionLog` row now, so half 1 finds both sites unaided: `CadenceFocusSupport.endSession`
  and `iOSFocusView.logBundleSession` are held in `existenceExemptions` naming this ticket, and
  `FocusView.bundleTimerControls` joined `timerControls` in `commitReachExemptions`. Fixing this
  means deleting those three names in the same change. The ledger also **downgrades the
  consequence**: a refused save leaves the row pending rather than destroying the minutes, and
  `CadenceFocusLedger.reconcile(in:)` puts the counter back once it lands. Still a defect — the
  reset still throws away the seconds the user is watching — but no longer an unrecoverable one.
  **CLOSED 2026-09-04 (`a1e5791`).** `CadenceFocusBundleSupport.distributeMinutes` takes a
  `commit:` and routes through `CadencePendingChangePersistence.commitEdit`, snapshotting every
  credited task's `BankedMinutes` before writing and restoring them in **reverse** order on refusal
  — forward order let a later task's already-mutated snapshot of a shared project counter win,
  caught by mutation testing. `endSession`, the bundle-shaped `logElapsedSeconds` and both
  `commitElapsed` overloads share this one commit; the timer only resets once it lands.
  `iOSFocusView`'s `select`/`toggleSession`/`logBundleSession`/`.onDisappear` catch a refusal and
  record it rather than clearing the clock. macOS's `FocusManager` gained the identical `commit:`
  plumbing — it previously wrote the pending bank with no `save()` of any kind, the worse of the two
  shapes this ticket named — and `FocusView`'s controls/log-session popovers report a refusal
  through `TaskCompletionAnimationManager.recordSettleFailure()`. The task-shaped pure-write helper
  `complete()` needs was renamed `logElapsedSeconds` → `bankElapsedSeconds`: the commit index needs
  every overload of a name to agree before it vouches for it, and one committing / one deliberately
  not was exactly the disagreement that made `logBundleSession`'s real commit invisible to the scan.
  Deleted the four `endSession`/`logBundleSession`/`bundleTimerControls`/`timerControls` exemption
  entries. Green across 4 targets; 3 mutations (reversed-restore removed, member-restore dropped,
  `addTask`'s old swallow reintroduced) killed.

- [T-664] **CLOSED 2026-09-05 (`65806e3`).** `successReport` gained a spelling for a surface that stays open and fills itself in: a write through a collection `@Binding`. The ticket's own experiment is now a killed mutation -- replanting `TagPickerPopoverViews.restore` exactly as it stood before [[T-652]] is **named** by the sweep, where T-664 had measured that the same replant left the suite green. Incomplete by design; see [[T-997]]. **Filed as:** **The `try? save()` rule's report vocabulary has no spelling for "the surface filled
  itself in".** Found — and then *measured* — while fixing [[T-652]].
  `CadenceSaveCommitRule.successReport` is a closed list of **dismissals**: `dismiss…()`,
  `is/show<X> = false`, `editing/selected/pending<X> = nil`, `presented<X> =`,
  `on(Save|Done|Complete|Commit)(`, plus `return true` from a `-> Bool` and a non-`nil` answer from
  a `-> X?`. That is exactly why [[T-497]] caught `TagPickerPopoverViews.saveEdits` and `.archive`
  — both end `editingTag = nil` — and did not catch `.restore`, which reports by **appending to a
  bound selection and blanking a search field**: `selectedTags.append(tag)`, `query = ""`. A
  surface that stays open and merely *fills in* is invisible to the rule.
  **Measured, not inferred.** Restoring the pre-fix `restore` as a mutation and re-running
  `CadenceSaveCommitDisciplineTests` left that suite **green**; only the new hand-written pin
  failed. And a scan of `Cadence/` at `4f74ff9` for the shape — a swallowed `save()` in a
  declaration that also `\w+.append(`s and also assigns `= ""` — found **exactly one** site, and it
  was `restore`. After the fix it is zero.
  **So this is a guard to add, not a backlog to work**, and its whole cost is false positives:
  `.append(` and `= ""` are far commoner than any dismissal, and the `pending<X> = nil` spelling
  already needed a `cancel()` discriminator to be worth two of them. Measure the false-positive
  count *before* widening; if the plain spelling costs more than it finds, scope it (a `@State` /
  `@Binding` target, or `= ""` only in a block that also appends).

For `CFBundleIconName` the macOS asset-catalog compiler injects the key regardless, but on iOS deleting the file's copy left it **missing entirely** from the built plist -- so there the file's copy was kept and the build setting removed.   while closing the review-hygiene half of [[T-626]]. The app target sets
  `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE = YES` **and** `INFOPLIST_FILE = Cadence/Info.plist`, and then spells
  `CFBundleIconName`, `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`, `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` and
  `NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription` as `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` build settings **as well as** in
  `Cadence/Info.plist`. Two sources of truth for four shipped values, and the usage strings are
  long sentences that App Review reads — editing one copy and shipping the other is a quiet way to
  ship the wrong words.

  (pick one home per key — the file, where the other five of its nine keys already live alone) does
  not depend on

  prevented is a second writer on the user's **preferences**. A debug build carries the same bundle id,
  so it gets the same sandbox container — `~/Library/Containers/com.haoranwei.Cadence/Data/`, exactly
  where the script's own header ([[T-1064]]) says the private store lands, and where
  `Data/tmp/CadenceUITestStores` exists (created 2026-09-07). `run-macos-app.sh` passes **no**
  `-CadenceSuiteName`, so `CadenceDefaults.store` in the launched instance resolves to
  `UserDefaults.standard`, i.e. the user's `Data/Library/Preferences/com.haoranwei.Cadence.plist`
  (**87 keys**, written the same day), and `Theme` / `CadenceWidgetRefreshCenter` reach the app-group
  suite `group.com.haoranwei.Cadence`, which `CadenceDefaults` documents as unroutable by design. So the
  guard is **correct for a reason it does not give**, and the reason it gives was handled before it fired.
  Filed as [[T-1157]], with the one-line fix and why it was not applied blind.
  **3. MEASURED — "what is open is whether to build the first one properly" is answered at HEAD.**
  `CadenceUITests/CadenceUITestPixelSupport.swift` reads an `XCUIScreenshot` as 8-bit sRGB RGBA;
  `CadenceTodayCompositionUITests` takes `window.screenshot()` and maps element frames onto its pixels;
  `CadenceUITestsLaunchTests` attaches `app.screenshot()`. The harness this ticket asks about exists.
  **4. MEASURED — that route has no guard on the user's app.** Nothing under `CadenceUITests/` and
  nothing in `scripts/xcb.sh` matches `/Applications/Cadence`. So "macOS visual verification is
  unavailable whenever the user's own Cadence is running" is **false as stated**: what is unavailable is
  `run-macos-app.sh`'s route. `docs/SUBAGENT_RUNBOOK.md`'s section repeated the same over-reach and is
  rewritten in this commit to say *"that route, not every route"*.
  **NOT MEASURED, and this is the honest limit of the closure.** No window screenshot of a second
  instance has actually been taken while the user's copy runs. The run was refused by a precondition
  unrelated to this ticket: `ioreg -n Root -d1 -k IOConsoleUsers` reported `"CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"=Yes`
  for the whole session, and `xcb.sh` exits 5 on a `CadenceUITests` run in that state ([[T-563]]). Point 4
  is therefore derived from source and from an absence, not from a picture. Carried as [[T-1158]] rather
  than smuggled into this closure as observation.

  stays 577pt in a 1194pt landscape host, the presentation is a fixed size and no iPad reaches

- [T-732] **CLOSED 2026-09-12 (agent `verifyenv`) — re-measured, and it went the other way: the premise's *conclusion* holds, its *mechanism* was wrong, and the item stays on the device list.**
  Originally: **`docs/device-checks.md`'s keyboard-dismiss item rests on a premise that is false on this
  fleet.** It says the simulator suppresses the software keyboard while a Mac keyboard is attached.
  OBSERVED 2026-09-02: the full software QWERTY came up unprompted in Cadence's new-task composer on
  the claimed iPad. If the keyboard is available, the `keyboardDismissMode = .interactive` check is a
  downward `touch_path` on the note text — a simulator job, not a phone one.

  item stayed on the hardware list for weeks because of an untested claim about the tooling rather than
  about the app. Re-triage before anyone carries it to a device.

  **CLOSED 2026-09-12 — re-derived on hardware this agent booted, and the 2026-09-02 reading did not
  reproduce.** iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5 (`7B642065-86FC-4987-8674-22066D32878C`), booted by
  `scripts/simulator-claim.sh boot --apply`, claimed and released in the same turn, left booted and
  untouched. **Simulator.app was not running** for any of it — `ps -Ao pid,command` matched nothing but
  Claude helpers — which is the first thing that makes the old wording wrong.
  **MEASURED, four readings.** (a) `ConnectHardwareKeyboard` appears **zero** times in the whole
  `com.apple.iphonesimulator` domain — not globally, and not in any of its per-device `DevicePreferences`
  entries — so nobody has ever set that toggle either way here. (b) In Spotlight, the search field took
  first responder (caret visible, Suggestions list up) and **no software keyboard was drawn**. (c) In
  **Safari's address bar**, same again: URL selected, field focused, no keyboard — two surfaces, one
  SpringBoard and one UIKit app. (d) Injected text lands anyway: `control text "abc"` wrote `Abc` into
  the Spotlight field and Settings answered *No Results for "Abc"*. A field that is first responder and
  accepts key events with nothing on screen **is** the suppression the item describes.
  **So the premise is materially right and mechanically wrong.** It is not that someone attached a Mac
  keyboard in Simulator.app; it is that a headless `simctl` boot comes up with one already attached and
  the agent surface cannot detach it — `xcrun simctl` has no keyboard command, and `simctl ui` offers
  appearance / increase_contrast / content_size only.
  **Fixed in this commit, in both places the false sentence lived.** `docs/device-checks.md` item 1 now
  states the headless-boot mechanism and names the one step that would unblock it (a person turning
  *I/O → Keyboard → Connect Hardware Keyboard* off in Simulator.app, which an agent may not do), and the
  same claim in `Cadence/iOS/iOSMarkdownEditor.swift`'s `keyboardDismissMode` comment — the more
  load-bearing copy, since it tells whoever debugs a stuck keyboard where to start — is corrected too.
  The cited line number there moved with the edit and was updated (`:170` → `:177`).
  **Two corrections of record.** The list is **two items, four steps, under two minutes**, and says so
  on its own line 7; a brief describing it as five items and five minutes is quoting the pre-[[T-561]]

  `CLAUDE.md` and every `AGENTS.md` by a tree walk and nothing else, and the only other mention in
  `CadenceTests/` is a doc comment in `MarkdownImagePasteTests` — so the [[T-732]] edit is safe for the
  reason that rule asks you to check, rather than by assumption.
  **Unsettled, deliberately: the iPad.** The 2026-09-02 reading was on one, and no iPad was booted here.
  Carried as [[T-1159]].

- [T-745] **CLOSED 2026-09-11 (`defaultsroute`) — the decision is *route them*, and the routing is a rule now instead of a set of correct call sites.** [[T-949]] is the same ticket and is closed as a duplicate. **27 sites across 12 files** now resolve through `CadenceDefaults.store`: `ListDetailView` x8, `PersistenceController` x6, `CadenceCalendarVisibilityPreferences` x3, `TasksPanel` x2, and one each in `NotificationManager`, `MarkdownNoteSupport`, `CadenceUITestSupport`, `PursuitToGoalMigration`, `AISettingsManager`, `AppleAccountManager`, `CadenceCalendarLinkObservations`, `CadenceNotesEditorPreferences`. Every one is a one-token substitution and **none of them changes the product**: with no `-CadenceSuiteName` argument `CadenceDefaults.store` *is* `UserDefaults.standard`, which is why this was safe to do to a hot file. **What it buys** is the thing neither filing had a name for: six keys were reachable through two stores at once — `notificationsEnabled`, `noteTemplateOverrides`, the hidden- and observed-calendar lists, the four `CadencePreferenceKeys` the UI-test reset clears, and the retired key `purgeRetiredKeys` drops — each written through a routed `@AppStorage` and read through an unrouted `.standard`, agreeing only because no launch argument was present. **Four sites are deliberately left, and the exemption is derived rather than typed**: `CadenceDefaults.swift` is in neither the `CadenceWidgets` nor the `CadenceMCPServer` Sources phase, so `Theme` and `CadenceWidgetRefreshCenter` (which reach the **app-group** suite on purpose — the widget is another process, and the accent id and the reload state are what both must agree about) and `DataIntegrityRepairService` and `NoteMigrationService` (in the CLI target's explicit list) physically cannot route. `CadenceDefaultsRoutingSweepTests.theSharedTargetExemptionNamesFilesTheRouterCannotReach` measures that premise both ways rather than asserting it. **The sweep was red before it was green**: run unchanged against `a92b659` it named exactly the twelve files the same commit routes, which is the only thing separating this census from one that matches nothing. The sweep's one stated limit: it reads spellings, so a bare `.standard` passed *positionally* into a `UserDefaults` parameter is invisible — `.standard` is also a `CadenceAccentPalette` case. The one site of that shape, `TasksPanel.storedSortMode(in: .standard, …)`, is why `in:` is one of the six needles. **The second gap this ticket raised is unchanged and now the only one left**: an app launched by tapping its icon on the simulator carries no launch arguments and is back on the device-wide domain. **Filed as:** **`CadenceDefaults` covers `@AppStorage` and the calendar memory, and nothing else.**
  [[T-735]] routed every `@AppStorage` through `defaultAppStorage` on the scene and pointed
  `CadenceCalendarDateMemory` at the same store, which is what the incident ran through. It does not
  reach the direct `UserDefaults.standard` calls in the service layer:
  `NotificationManager.reconcile`'s `notificationsEnabled` read, `DataIntegrityRepairService`'s
  `dataIntegrityRepair.lastReport.v1`, `MarkdownNoteSupport`'s `NoteTemplateLibrary.storageKey`,
  `PursuitToGoalMigration`'s completion flag, `PersistenceController`'s pending/failed-restore
  records, and `CadenceUITestSupport.resetUserDefaults`. Most already take a `defaults:` parameter
  defaulted to `.standard`, so the change is mechanical — but `PersistenceController.swift` is a hot
  file and `NotificationManager` cannot exist in the command-line target, so it wants doing
  deliberately rather than as a sweep.
  Second gap, same family, cheaper to state than to fix: **an app started by tapping its icon on the
  simulator carries no launch arguments**, so it is back on the device-wide domain. Both are written
  down in `CadenceDefaults`'s doc comment; this ticket is the decision about whether to close them.
  **Answered in part 2026-09-05, still open.** [[T-949]] re-counted this audit directly against HEAD and
  found the product half is a non-issue: `CadenceDefaults.store` **is** `UserDefaults.standard` unless a
  `-CadenceSuiteName` launch argument is present, and nothing outside `scripts/simulator-claim.sh` sets
  one — so none of the 19 direct `UserDefaults.standard` sites diverge in any shipping configuration.
  What landed is that measurement; **what remains is this ticket's actual ask** — the decision whether to
  route those sites anyway, and no code has changed (`NotificationManager`, `DataIntegrityRepairService`,
  `MarkdownNoteSupport`, `PersistenceController` still read `.standard` directly). The test-tooling

- [T-748] **CLOSED 2026-09-04 (`f3a7fba1`) - the head checks its own pulse before taking the
  lock.** `test-host-lock.sh acquire`'s head-of-queue block now refuses `mkdir` (and drops its own
  ticket) if `$PPID` -- the caller blocking on `acquire` -- is dead, exactly the four-line fix
  [[T-650]] named and deliberately left out.
  **Failing-first, measured, and a real orphan, not a killed process**: a wrapper spawns `acquire` as
  a genuine child (`; :` stops zsh exec'ing it in the wrapper's place, same trick as the selftest's
  `waiter()`), only the wrapper is killed, and the lock is released to the now-parentless acquire.
  Against `git show HEAD:scripts/test-host-lock.sh` it takes the lock (`owner='orphan'`); against the
  fix it declines (`owner=''`) and the queue drains.
  Selftest gained `dead-parent-declines` and `dead-parent-recovers` (the latter proving the queue
  does not stall behind a waiter that declined), alongside [[T-650]]'s three.

  Gained a `selftest` mode of its own (this script had none before), proving `ordering` and

  Both `test-host-lock.sh` and `simulator-claim.sh`'s selftests are now wired into

- [T-959] **CLOSED 2026-09-12 (agent `sandboxzsh`).** The broad reading is FALSE and three decisions rested on it; what the host refuses is narrower and sharper than "cannot spawn", and is now measured and pinned by `CadenceTestHostSandboxCapabilityTests` rather than described. **Originally:** **CadenceTests' App-Sandboxed host cannot spawn `ps` or `pgrep` at all -- EPERM at
  `posix_spawn`, not merely restricted output.** Found landing [[T-748]]/[[T-749]]'s selftests in
  `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests`. [[T-782]] closed a narrower version of this as moot: the only
  two shell-outs under `CadenceTests` at the time (`CadenceSelftestRun.of`'s `/bin/zsh -f <script>
  selftest`, and `.probe()`'s `/bin/echo` control) both target working tools, so there was no
  populated case of a broken one. This is the general rule that closure did not establish.
  Measured 2026-09-04: `Process().run()` on `/bin/ps` from inside `CadenceTests` throws `Error
  Domain=NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=1 "Operation not permitted"` before producing a single byte of
  output -- an outright launch refusal, not empty output -- and a `zsh` child of that host inherits
  the same sandbox, so a script's own internal `ps -o command= -p $pid` or `pgrep -f ...` fails
  identically once it is spawned as this test target's descendant.
  `test-host-lock.sh`'s `waiter_alive` (`ps`) and `live_test_hosts` (`pgrep`), and
  `simulator-claim.sh`'s `waiter_alive` (ported from the same file), all depend on one of these --
  which is why `ordering` (both scripts) and `no-reclaim` (`test-host-lock.sh`) cannot be proven from
  `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests` and are TOLERATED there by name (see that suite's
  `testHostLockPropertiesUnverifiableInThisSandbox` / `simulatorClaimPropertiesUnverifiableInThisSandbox`)
  rather than asserted dishonestly.
  Separately, but found the same afternoon and the same family: a freshly-written, freshly-`chmod
  +x`'d script cannot always be exec'd DIRECTLY from inside this host either --
  `simulator-claim.sh selftest`'s fake `simctl` died with "can't create temp file for here document"
  (the `$TMPPREFIX` issue [[T-782]]/[[T-719]] already named) until routed through `/bin/zsh <path>`
  rather than executing the path itself. Distinct mechanism from the `ps`/`pgrep` finding, same
  family: this host can run a trusted binary and hand it a path, and cannot always spawn an arbitrary
  one of its own, no cross-process introspection.
  Any future selftest wired into this suite that needs either should expect the same wall: tolerate
  it by name (the pattern above), and prove that property by direct terminal invocation instead --
  which is what [[T-748]] and [[T-749]]'s entries above do.

  **MEASURED 2026-09-12 (macOS 26.6 / Xcode 26.6), from inside a real `CadenceTests` run, 24 probes.**
  Every line below is a spawn attempted by the test host itself and its outcome read back out of the
  test log -- none of it is reasoned from the sandbox profile.

  **What this host CAN do.** It spawns `/bin/echo`, `/bin/ls`, `/usr/bin/env`, `/bin/sh` and
  `/bin/zsh` freely, and a `zsh` three levels deep still runs -- which is how
  `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests` already runs six guard-script selftests, the point `gatefigure2`
  made closing [[T-986]]. It spawns **Xcode's own `xcodebuild`** (`-version`, exit 0, *"Xcode 26.6"*).
  It execs **a script that was already on disk directly**: `./scripts/xcb.sh` prints its usage and
  exits 2. It reads the checkout it is testing. It writes inside its own container `$TMPDIR`,
  including `mktemp -d`.

  **What it CANNOT do, and the actual mechanism in each case -- three different ones, not one.**

  1. **A setuid binary is refused at `posix_spawn`.** `/bin/ps` (`4755`) and `/usr/bin/top` (`4555`)
     both throw `NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=1` before a byte of output. That half of this ticket is
     correct, and the mechanism is the setuid bit -- not the identity of `ps`.
  2. **`pgrep` is NOT in that class and this ticket was simply wrong about it.** `/usr/bin/pgrep` is
     `755`, spawns perfectly well, and exits 3 saying *"sysmon request failed with error: sysmond
     service not found / pgrep: Cannot get process list"*. It is denied the process **list**, not
     the **exec**. In-process the same wall by the same mechanism: `proc_listpids` returns 0 with
     `errno=EPERM`. This is the worse of the two failures, not the milder one -- a refusal announces
     itself, and an answer of zero does not.
  3. **A file this process itself wrote cannot be exec'd, whatever it is.** A freshly written,
     freshly `chmod 755`'d script: EPERM. A **byte-for-byte, non-setuid copy of `/bin/ls`**, 0755:
     EPERM. Handing either path to `/bin/zsh` works. So this is not the here-document `$TMPPREFIX`
     issue [[T-782]]/[[T-719]] found -- that is real and separate (a bare here-document still fails
     with *"can't create temp file for here document"* until `TMPPREFIX` is moved inside `$TMPDIR`)
     -- and it is not `mutate.sh`'s "an unrecognised exec target" either, which the repo's own
     scripts execing fine disproves.

  Two more, neither previously on the record and both load-bearing: **the `/usr/bin` xcrun shims run
  and then refuse** -- `git`, `python3` and `/usr/bin/xcodebuild` all spawn and print *"xcrun: error:
  cannot be used within an App Sandbox"*, a different failure with a different fix from either of the
  above -- and **writes land in its container and nowhere else**: `/tmp` is EPERM, and so is the
  checkout under test, while reading that checkout is fine.

  **Which decisions rested on the broad reading.** Three, and the accounting matters more than the
  probe does.

  * **The `ordering` / `no-reclaim` tolerations in `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests` (from
    [[T-748]]/[[T-749]]) SURVIVE, on corrected and partly stronger grounds.** `ordering` really is
    the setuid-`ps` refusal: `waiter_alive` reads an empty command line and calls every waiter dead.
    `no-reclaim` is not a refusal at all -- `live_test_hosts` pipes a running `pgrep`'s empty output
    into `wc -l` and gets a plausible `0`. Same verdict, different mechanism, and the second one is
    a live hazard rather than a testing inconvenience: filed as [[T-1152]]. The doc comments on
    `testHostLockPropertiesUnverifiableInThisSandbox`, `theTestHostLocksOwnGuardsStillFire` and
    `theSimulatorClaimsOwnGuardStillFires` are corrected here to say which is which.
  * **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s reason for [[T-977]] is FALSIFIED as written.** It says the host
    *"cannot spawn `xcodebuild`, ps or pgrep at all"*; two of those three are wrong. Whether an
    in-host run is genuinely impossible now rests on the container write restriction instead, which

    generalisation written beside it ("ps/pgrep are not special cases; an unrecognised exec target
    is") is wrong in both directions and is corrected. `mutate.sh selftest`: 70 passed, 0 failed.

    <script>` and fails for a `$TMPDIR` reason rather than T-959's. That was the one place the broad
    reading had already been noticed, and it was right.

  **The instrument, and why it is a test and not a paragraph.** `CadenceTestHostSandboxCapabilityTests`
  (6 tests) asserts the matrix in both directions -- that `ps` and `top` are setuid AND refused, that
  `pgrep`, `zsh` and `ls` are NOT setuid AND spawn, that a self-written file is refused while the
  repo's own script is not, that `proc_listpids` answers nothing, that `/tmp` and the checkout are
  unwritable while the container is writable. Each assertion carries the observation that would
  falsify it, so an OS that lifts one of these limits turns this suite red instead of leaving a
  six-day-old sentence in a ledger to be generalised from again. That failure mode is what this
  ticket cost: the sentence was measured once, correctly, on one binary, and then read as a rule.

  - **Columns are written through the container's own `sectionConfigs` setter, not through

    list's single JSON blob; a container inserted one line earlier has no second holder and no

    own doc comment names. It is also not in `CadenceMCPServer`'s explicit Sources phase, and
    adding a `Shared/` file there to reach a no-op is the coupling that guide warns about.
  - **Refusals where the app forgives.** `Area.normalizedSectionConfigs` silently drops a blank
    column name and a case-insensitive duplicate, and `TagSupport.normalizedColorHex` silently
    falls back on a bad hex. Both are right beside a UI the user is watching and wrong as an answer
    to an API request, which sees only the word "success" — so all three are `throw`s here, on the
    same argument `CadenceMCPServiceSupport.normalizedSectionName` already makes about a mistyped
    section. `areaId` and `dueDate` sent to an `area` are refused on the *requested text*, before
    resolution, so the error is about the shape rather than about an id.

    optional-to-optional `nil == nil` unfiled bucket. Not cosmetic: `CadenceMCPOrdering.precedes`
    breaks an `order` tie on the *name*, so a row left at the model default of 0 would interleave
    alphabetically with the user's own rather than landing where it was created.
  - **A `Default` column always exists**, synthesised by the container normaliser, so
    `sectionNames: ["Backlog", "Doing"]` yields three columns. The advertised schema says so rather
    than letting a caller find out.

Guide text is flattened on whitespace first, because a citation wrapped across a line at ~100 columns would otherwise make the pin pass or fail on where the wrap landed ("Why three\n  kinds have no constructor" is exactly that case, today, in the MCP guide). `pinnedHeadings` is the weaker fallback for `Cadence/iOS/AGENTS.md`, the one guide that links its reference without naming a section. **Mutation-verified, both directions**: renaming `## Why Three Kinds Have No Constructor` in the reference and re-pointing the guide's link both turn the suite red, with the messages *"docs/MCP_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md has no heading for \"Why three kinds have no constructor\", which CadenceMCPServer/AGENTS.md still sends readers to"* and *"CadenceMCPServer/AGENTS.md never routes to ../docs/MCP_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md"*. `theGuideReferencePairingTableIsNotVacuous` guards the empty-string case every one of those assertions is otherwise satisfied by. **Runs:** `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`, 1044 swift compile tasks, 0 warnings, `AgentContextBudgetTests` green at 8 tests. **Original filing:** **`docs/MCP_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md` is the only one of the four long references that no test pins, so the guide it exists for can quietly stop linking to it.** Filed 2026-09-13 by `mcpguide`, which created it while closing [[T-1208]]. `AgentContextBudgetTests` asserts the pairing for the other three by name — `activeAgentGuidesStayCompactAndRouteToReferences` checks that root `AGENTS.md` contains `docs/AGENTS_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/CONTEXT_INDEX.md`, that `Cadence/Shared/AGENTS.md` contains `../../docs/SHARED_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md` and that `Cadence/iOS/AGENTS.md` contains `../../docs/IOS_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md`, and `longAgentReferencesRemainExplicitlyArchived` pins a section heading in each of the three files so a gutted reference goes red. Neither names the MCP pair. **Why that matters here specifically:** the cap that forced this split will force the next one too, and the failure mode it creates is a reference nobody is routed to — the exact "unpinned and unrouted" gap T-434 was filed about, one file later. The fix is two lines in the existing tests (`CadenceMCPServer/AGENTS.md` contains `../docs/MCP_AGENTS_REFERENCE.md`; that file contains a heading such as `## Why The Prohibition Was Wrong`), and worth doing as a loop over a pairs table rather than a fourth hand-written clause, since the hand-written list is why three of four were covered and the fourth was not.

- [T-1209] **CLOSED 2026-09-13 (agent `ledgerguard`) — the script re-syncs the copy nobody could lose, and names on stderr the one it must not touch.** Originally filed as: **A successful `<path>=<content-file>` commit leaves the worktree copy of that path behind HEAD, and nothing says so or guards the READING of it.** Filed 2026-09-13 by `ledgerheal2`, observed on its own commit. **MEASURED at `b34c1f5`:** `scripts/agent-commit.sh ledgerheal2 -m … docs/TODO.md=<file> docs/TODO_DONE.md=<file>` reported `committed b34c1f5b` and `shared index is clean against the new HEAD`, and immediately afterwards both worktree files were **byte-identical to `HEAD~1`** — the whole commit was in the tree and in neither file on disk. The behaviour is almost certainly deliberate and right: the `=` form exists for a file a sibling is also editing, and writing the worktree would destroy their in-flight hunks. The gap is that the committing agent is never told to re-sync its own, and `docs/SUBAGENT_RUNBOOK.md`'s *"Which path form to use"* section — which explains `REBUILD-BEHIND-HEAD`, `DECLINED-HUNK-LOST` and why never to `git commit -- <path>` — does not mention it at all.
  **The commit path is already guarded; the read path is not.** A later bare-`<path>` commit of the stale file is refused by `WORKTREE-BEHIND-HEAD`, and a reconstruction built the documented way (`git show HEAD:<path>` plus your edits) is correct by construction. What nothing catches is an agent that **reads** `docs/TODO.md` off disk to find work, or to quote an entry, or to count the Open section — it gets the previous revision with no signal, and in this repository that file is the ledger, the id allocator and the work queue at once. The one-line cure is `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>` after the commit; the question is whether `agent-commit.sh` should do it for paths whose worktree copy is byte-identical to the revision it just replaced (i.e. where no sibling edit can be lost), or whether the runbook should simply say to do it by hand.
  **Fixed 2026-09-13 in `scripts/agent-commit.sh` step 5b, on exactly the condition this entry proposed.** After the commit lands, a `=` path whose worktree copy is **byte-identical to the revision the commit replaced** is written back from what just landed — nobody's edits can be in a copy that equals the revision being replaced — and the run says so. Any other copy is left untouched and named **on stderr**, with the cure printed: *read `git show HEAD:<path>`, never the file on disk, and re-sync with `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`*. Overwriting that second copy would destroy the sibling hunks the `=` form exists to protect, so the conditional is the fix and an unconditional write-back would be a new bug.
  `docs/SUBAGENT_RUNBOOK.md`'s *"Which path form to use"* section now carries this, and [[T-1206]] and [[T-1207]] with it.
  **Proved by mutation, not by watching it pass.** Removing the write-back (the behaviour before this commit) killed 1 check; dropping the safety condition so a sibling's in-flight copy is overwritten killed 2. Mode 4j in `scripts/agent-commit.sh selftest`.

What is added is `CadenceTypographyScaleTests.theTwoTitleRolesAreTwoRolesAndNotOneRoleAtTwoBases`, which pins all three differences plus the published ceilings (49/22, 47/20) and the merge cost, so a future convergence has to argue with the evidence rather than with the count; and the decision is written on `CadenceTypographyRole.composerTitle` where the old 'documented outlier' note was. An MCP completion of the focused task now ends or advances the Mac's Focus session when the app adopts the write.** The out-of-process write never touches the app's copy of the row, so T-5310's `statusRaw` watch has nothing to fire on. `macOSRootView.refreshAppData()` swaps in a fresh context and `macOSRootDataRefreshSupport.adoptReplacementContext` re-points the session at the live row, which is already DONE. The watch re-arms on that row and waits for a change that already happened. Measured red before the fix by `CadenceRootContextSwapAdoptionTests.aFocusedTaskCompletedByAnotherProcessReleasesTheSessionWhenTheSwapAdoptsIt`. That test opens two `ModelContainer`s on one on-disk temp store and makes `CadenceWriteService.completeTask`'s mutation (`CadenceTaskRecurrenceWorkflowSupport.markDone` + save) through the second, without its audit log or app-group marker. It then runs `CadenceModelContextRefresh.replacement` + `adoptReplacementContext`. Before the fix the session stayed on the done task, 0 minutes were banked and the clock kept running (3 failed expectations). The app's own copy of the row also stayed open until the swap. **Fix:** `adoptReplacementContext` now calls `focusManager.releaseIfActiveTaskSettled()` after re-resolving (`Cadence/macOS/Views/macOSRootDataRefreshSupport.swift`), the same bank-and-move-on as the in-process watch. A session whose row was deleted keeps the old open object, so it is still kept rather than cleared. **Mutation:** dropping that call reddens the new test alone (baseline green over 5). **Not verified:** a real `CadenceMCPServer` process, CloudKit-imported changes, and the 0.2 s `NSApp.isActive` gate before the swap: the release waits until the app is next active. **Originally:** **OPEN 2026-10-24 (filed by agent `strand0337` from its range under [[T-5891]], split out of [[T-5310]]; NOT run, NOT SEEN ON SCREEN; a verification gap, not an observed defect) -- it is unknown whether completing the focused task through MCP (the separate `CadenceMCPServer` process) releases the Mac's Focus session the way an in-app completion now does.** [[T-5310]]'s fix is a `withObservationTracking` watch on the focused `AppTask` instance's `statusRaw` (`Cadence/macOS/Services/FocusManager.swift`, `watchActiveTaskStatus`). An in-process write to that instance fires it (tested). A write from another process reaches the app only as a store change merged into its context; whether that merge mutates the same model instance's observed property -- and so fires the watch -- is unmeasured, and `mactask2308` flagged the same gap. **To settle:** a test that writes the status through a second `ModelContext`/container on the same store and merges, then asserts the session moved; if it does not fire, re-check `activeTask` when the app's context merges a remote change. DECISION-FREE.

- [T-6001] **CLOSED 2026-10-24 (agent `iossheets1420`, the commit carrying this line; built and unit-tested on the macOS leg with the iOS build leg green, 0 warnings on both; NOT SEEN ON SCREEN -- no simulator was driven and no app was evicted) -- option (a) landed: the iOS focus session is persisted and RESUMED LIVE on next open. `CadenceFocusSessionPersistence` (`Cadence/Shared/`) keeps `{taskID, isRunning, startedAt, accumulatedSeconds}` as JSON under `ios.focus.session` in `CadenceDefaults.store`; `iOSFocusView` writes it from ONE place, `.onChange(of: sessionRecord)`, so the play control, a pick row, a handoff, Complete and Reset all persist without each remembering to, and restores it in `onAppear` BEFORE the handoff branch, so a handoff arriving in the same breath banks the resumed session through `accept(_:)` rather than dropping it. `isRunning` is stored as well as the two the decision names, because a PAUSED session has `startedAt == nil` and seconds on the clock and must come back paused rather than start counting on its own.  FULL `CadenceTests` run at `eda890d8` (the commit after which all three of these landed): **6642 tests in 620 suites PASSED** in 415.8s, with one pre-existing known issue (`CadenceTestTargetHygieneTests.aMalformedSuiteRulePatternIsReportedNotTreatedAsClean`, a deliberate `withKnownIssue` at `TemporaryDefaultsSupport.swift:505`), 0 warnings; the iOS build leg at the same sha is non-vacuous and clean (1418 Swift compile tasks, 0 errors, 0 warnings). Amended by the commit carrying this line.**Nothing here writes to the SwiftData store.** Minutes are still banked by exactly one path, `CadenceFocusSupport.endSession`, on exactly the exits that already called it; this ticket persists a NOTE of what is on the clock, so losing it loses a resume and never a banked minute. The record is cleared on the success side of `onDisappear`'s `do`, never in the `catch` -- T-654's rule said in the new store: over a refused bank `timerState` is left where it was and the record with it, so the session is still there to retry. A record naming a task that is gone, done or cancelled resolves to nothing and is cleared, asked through `CadenceFocusSupport.canFocus` -- the picker's own predicate -- so a task finished on the Mac while the phone was closed does not come back under a running clock (T-276, T-5310). Restore is the COLD route only (`guard !timerState.isRunning, accumulatedSeconds == 0`), because `onAppear` fires again on re-entry and a clock already standing is the live session. An idle clock is never persisted, so visiting Focus does not write a zero against whatever heads the picker. The filing's references held exactly: `iOSFocusView.swift:18`, `:119`, `CadenceFocusPlanningSupport.swift:20-45`, and there is still no `scenePhase` handler in the file -- a test now asserts there is none, since option (b) was declined. Pinned by `CadenceFocusSessionPersistenceTests` (10 tests, green -- an earlier revision of this line said 9, which was a miscount of the file rather than a run). Mutations KILLED 3/3, each compiled. RESIDUAL filed as [[T-6223]]: resuming live means the clock is wall-clock across the gap, so a force-quit at night reopens in the morning reading eleven hours -- which is the exact reading [[T-1103]] added the Mac's sleep pause to prevent. The owner decided the resume; what a LONG gap should do was not put to them. Originally: OPEN 2026-10-24 (filed by agent `audit0708` from its range under [[T-5990]]; read against source, NOT run, NOT SEEN ON SCREEN; rank 2; NEEDS-DECISION) -- on iPhone and iPad a running Focus session lives only in view state, so if iOS evicts or the user swipes away the backgrounded app, the clock and every unlogged minute are gone with no log written; the Mac banks on quit ([[T-5305]]).** Evidence: `@State private var timerState = CadenceFocusTimerState()` (`Cadence/iOS/iOSFocusView.swift:18`); `CadenceFocusTimerState` is a plain value with `startedAt`/`accumulatedSeconds` and no persistence (`Cadence/Shared/CadenceFocusPlanningSupport.swift:20-45`); the only banking exit is `.onDisappear` (`iOSFocusView.swift:119`), which does not run on process termination; no `scenePhase` handler in the file. T-5305 itself recorded the iOS case as "Not checked". User steps: start a session on iPhone, switch to other apps for a long while (or force-quit) -> reopen -> Focus at 00:00, nothing added to the task's actual time. Fix shape (the decision): either persist `{target, startedAt, accumulatedSeconds}` in `CadenceDefaults.store` and restore on appear (session survives), or bank on `scenePhase == .background` (log partial, restart clean). Lease: `iOSFocusView.swift` and `CadenceFocusPlanningSupport.swift` both LEASED; both CLEAN. Ledger searched for iOS Focus + kill/terminate/background/scenePhase: no duplicate. **OWNER DECISION 2026-10-24 (recorded by the coordinator from the owner's answer in session; no code written yet): OPTION (a) -- PERSIST `{target, startedAt, accumulated}` AND RESUME THE LIVE SESSION ON NEXT OPEN.** Option (b), banking a partial log on `scenePhase == .background`, was declined for the stated reason: it would end the session every time the user glances at another app, which is most of how a phone is used. A running Focus session must survive eviction and a force-quit, as it already does on the Mac. Size M, the largest of this batch.

Evidence: the only thing that mints a next occurrence is `spawnNextOccurrenceIfNeeded`, reached only from `markDone` and `markCancelled` (`Cadence/Shared/CadenceTaskRecurrenceWorkflowSupport.swift:24-55`, `:138`). A delete runs `repairDanglingRecurrenceLinks` (`:102-120`, called from `CadenceTaskMutationSupport.deleteTasks`, `Cadence/Shared/CadenceTaskMutationSupport.swift:827`), which only clears or re-points the settled predecessor's pointer, so with the live occurrence gone nothing ever spawns again unless the user reopens and re-completes an old occurrence. The confirmations say nothing about the series: macOS "This will permanently delete \"<title>\"." (`Cadence/macOS/Services/DeleteConfirmationManager.swift:157-158`), iOS "This removes the task and its subtasks." (`Cadence/iOS/iOSTaskViews.swift:161-162`, `Cadence/iOS/iOSTaskDetailSheet.swift:132-133`). Cancel already means "skip this one, keep the series" (`markCancelled`'s doc), but a user who deletes today's occurrence to skip it loses every future one. User steps: daily repeating task -> delete today's occurrence -> confirm -> it never comes back. Fix shape (the decision): (a) say it -- for a recurring task the confirmation adds "This also ends the repeat; use Cancel to skip one occurrence." (copy-only, lease-free on macOS, leased on iOS); or (b) offer the two scopes the edit dialogs already use, "Delete This Occurrence" (spawns the successor, then deletes) / "Delete Series". Ledger searched (delete + series/recurring/occurrence, `repairDanglingRecurrenceLinks`, in TODO.md and TODO_DONE.md at HEAD): only mechanics entries about the pointer repair; no ticket on the user-visible loss. Files: `Cadence/macOS/Services/DeleteConfirmationManager.swift` lease-free, CLEAN; `Cadence/Shared/CadenceTaskRecurrenceWorkflowSupport.swift` lease-free, CLEAN; `Cadence/iOS/iOSTaskViews.swift`, `Cadence/iOS/iOSTaskDetailSheet.swift`, `Cadence/Shared/CadenceTaskMutationSupport.swift` all LEASED (exact-path patterns), all CLEAN. **OWNER DECISION 2026-10-25** (recorded by the coordinator in the commit carrying this line; asked and answered in session, nothing built yet) -- DECIDED, and the LARGEST of the four options: OFFER THE CHOICE. A delete on a repeating task asks whether it means THIS OCCURRENCE or THE WHOLE SERIES, the way Calendar does, and deleting one occurrence LEAVES THE REPEAT ALIVE. This is the only option on the table where a repeat survives a delete, and the owner took it over the cheap copy-only fix. Both confirmations have to carry it -- `DeleteConfirmationManager.swift:157` on macOS and the two iOS sites (`iOSTaskViews.swift:161`, `iOSTaskDetailSheet`) -- and "this occurrence" must actually spawn the next one, which today only `markDone` and `markCancelled` do via `spawnNextOccurrenceIfNeeded`. A non-repeating task must not grow a second button. Size M, and the series-ending path is what `repairDanglingRecurrenceLinks` already half-implements.
  - **RC-TRIAGE 2026-10-25 (agent `rctriage0710`): POST-RC** -- deleting the open occurrence of a repeating task ends the series without saying so; an explicit user delete with long-standing behaviour, recoverable by re-completing an old occurrence, and the fix is copy or a scope dialog. The closest call to the data-loss line in this triage, worth doing early after the RC.

A `touch_path` that holds stationary for 0.8s or 1.5s and then drags does not lift a Calendar timed block; the timeline scrolls instead. A second hunk fixes the same mechanism on the other axis, found while verifying: `width * progress` plus 12pt of padding is wider than the block at a full fill, and an over-wide ZStack child dragged the whole stack -- wash and border included -- 6pt sideways; progress is now measured against the inset track. Pixel evidence, same device, same tap, 30fps capture diffed row-by-row against rest: BEFORE, the capsule's own row held 0 pixels above G=100 at every frame of the fill; AFTER, rows y=903..907 read dG +100..+110 against a wash peaking at 59, and the band grows 132 -> 329 -> 526 -> 828 -> 946 px across the fill with its near end fixed on the 6pt inset. The invariant that distinguishes them is that the NEAR end is anchored on the inset and must not move between a quarter, a two-thirds and a full fill. - [T-3334] **CLOSED 2026-10-22 (coordinator, read-only census; answers the owner's question "could we run two test hosts at once" with a NO for now, and says what the real blocker is) -- splitting the host-free tests into a second, un-hosted target is NOT cheap, and the reason is the module structure rather than the test host.** **The question.** One global test-host lock means one macOS test runs at a time ([[T-236]]): `CadenceTests` is hosted INSIDE `Cadence.app` (`TEST_HOST = $(BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR)/Cadence.app/...`), the app is sandboxed, and macOS keys the container on the BUNDLE ID, so every run shares `~/Library/Containers/com.haoranwei.Cadence/Data/` no matter where DerivedData points. A second lane needs a second container, hence a second bundle id. **What was measured.** The host-dependency census says the hosted-ness is NOT the obstacle: of **455** test files, only **16 (3%)** name `Bundle.main`, `NSApplication`/`UIApplication`, `containerURL` or the app group at all. **The obstacle is linkage.** **434 of the 455 files use `@testable import Cadence`**, and `grep productType` over the project shows there is **no framework or library target** -- only application, app-extension, unit-test, ui-testing and tool. The app's code lives entirely in the app target, which is exactly WHY `@testable import Cadence` resolves: the test bundle is loaded into the app. Un-host a test and that import has nothing to bind to. **So the genuinely movable set today is 21 files** (those that do not import the app at all), **17 of them source-scan tests** whose helper `CadenceSourceScanSupport.swift` lives in the test target rather than the app. Moving 21 of 455 leaves 434 still serialised behind the one lock, which buys nothing worth the change. **Therefore:** a second lane requires extracting the app's code into a framework or library target that both the app and an un-hosted test bundle can link -- the big structural refactor already deferred until after the RC -- or per-agent bundle ids, which drags in the app group, the CloudKit container `iCloud.com.haoranwei.Cadence` and provisioning profiles in the owner's Apple Developer account under `CODE_SIGN_STYLE = Automatic`. **A correction, recorded because the coordinator said otherwise before measuring:** this option was described to the owner as "additive, reversible, and needs no account changes". The additive and reversible half is wrong -- it is gated on a refactor of how every source file is compiled. The census above is what should have been run before saying it. **What to do instead, and it is already ticketed:** [[T-3287]] records `CadenceGuardScriptSelftestTests` at **278-282 s over 44 tests**, nearly all of it in two tests (`theTestHostLocksOwnGuardsStillFire` 137 s, `theCommitHelpersOwnGuardsStillFire` 95 s), with the probe seeing only 2,212 file reads at 0.15 s and no derivation -- so the time is not scanning and [[T-3261]]'s cache cannot reach it. Making the suite shorter needs no architecture change and is worth more per hour than a second lane. [[T-3286]] is the next one after it. [[T-236]] [[T-3287]] **ADDENDUM 2026-10-22 (provenance, and a worked example of the hazard this ledger keeps describing): this entry's text was written by the coordinator but is CARRIED BY `49c8e863`, a commit whose subject is T-3250/T-3229 and whose message does not mention T-3334 at all.** The entry was sitting un-committed in the shared worktree when another agent staged `docs/TODO.md` whole to land its own two closures, and `agent-commit.sh` stages WHOLE FILES -- so a sibling's in-flight work rode along silently, which is [[T-1385]] / `d65d294` exactly. Nothing was lost and the text is byte-complete; only the attribution is wrong, which is why this is an addendum rather than a re-file. **The symmetry is the point:** minutes earlier the coordinator avoided doing this TO that same agent by committing `docs/TODO.md` through the `<path>=<content-file>` form after spotting their longer T-3250 and T-3229 lines in the worktree. The `=` form is the whole defence, it is cheap, and the cost of skipping it is a commit that silently contains someone else's work.

`.claude/worktrees/` never reached that walk only because hidden entries are already filtered, which is why [[T-3241]] did not see it. **THE CATEGORY IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT THE COUNT, AND IT SPLITS THREE WAYS.** **(i) Two of the three break on a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy of HEAD, with nothing edited.** `AgentContextBudgetTests.everyScopedAgentGuideIsRoutedFromTheRootGuide` asserts `root.contains("`\(guide)`")` over the path SET, so a faithful copy of the twelve scoped guides is twelve failures asking the root guide why it does not route to another tree's copy of itself; `CadenceAgentDefaultsIsolationTests.everySiteThatRedirectsTheStoreAlsoRefusesTheOwnersICloud` asserts `swiftWrites.count == 1` against a UNIQUE expected path, so one copied `CadenceUITests/CadenceUITestEnvironment.swift` is enough. A hazard that needs no mistake to fire is a different class from one that does. **(ii) [[T-3330]]'s own caller is the by-basename shape:** an index that resolves only a unique match returns nothing at all once every basename doubles. **(iii) `CadenceBuildInvocationHygieneTests.scannedPaths()` is CONTENT-dependent and the weakest of the three**, which is why it is reported as such rather than counted with them: it sweeps full relative paths and asserts `offenders.isEmpty`, so a byte-identical copy stays GREEN and only an EDITED one reddens it -- which is exactly what a scratch tree is for. It is also the one that needs no tree at all: it reads `scratchpad/<id>/*.md` and `*.sh` loose agent notes TODAY, and there were 84 files under `scratchpad/` when this was written. **MEASURED, three legs, on a probe at `scratchpad/probe-treeprune/tree/` built by `git show HEAD:<path>` -- 12 `AGENTS.md` (`cmp`-identical to HEAD's), `CadenceUITests/CadenceUITestEnvironment.swift` (identical), and one `docs/direct-distribution-runbook.md` with `-derivedDataPath` dropped from its archive command, standing in for the mutation edit a scratch tree exists to hold. No `.git` inside it, so `isNestedCheckout` cannot see it.** **RED (prunes reverted, probe standing, still tree):** `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=65`, 0 warnings, 3 swift compile tasks, 90 test result lines, 16 issues in 4 suites -- `everyScopedAgentGuideIsRoutedFromTheRootGuide` **12** issues, `everySiteThatRedirectsTheStoreAlsoRefusesTheOwnersICloud` 1 (`swiftWrites.count == 1`), `everyDocumentedBuildInvocationNamesAPrivateDerivedDataPath` 1 (`offenders.isEmpty`), and the new census 2. **GREEN (prunes applied, THE SAME PROBE STILL STANDING):** `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`, 0 warnings, 9 swift compile tasks, 74 test result lines, iOS leg `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`. **CONTROL (probe removed, prunes applied):** `XCODEBUILD_EXIT=0`, 74 test result lines -- the same 74 as the green leg, which is what says the probe was the only variable. Its `warnings: 0` is flagged `VACUOUS-COUNT` and is NOT quoted as warning evidence: removing the probe changed no Swift file, so that run compiled 0 of them. **The non-vacuous warning count is the GREEN leg's** -- 9 swift compile tasks, 0 warnings, over all four edited files. **The first red leg is not the one quoted**, and the reason is recorded rather than dropped: it carried `tree changed during this run (T-3060)` (`47141c3a` -> `b664ed08`) AND the new census test never executed, because it had been inserted into `CadenceSourceScanReaderTests` -- the suite that happens to occupy lines 109-393 of `CadenceTestTargetHygieneTests.swift` -- which was not in the `-only-testing` list. A file holding several suites is exactly the T-1076 shape, and `PARTIAL-SCOPE` said so in both result blocks while the run still read as a clean red. The test was moved into `CadenceTestTargetHygieneTests` and both legs re-run on a still tree. **A CENSUS RATHER THAN A SEVENTH DOC COMMENT.** [[T-3241]] turned four hand-written prune lists into one argument and warned that *"four copies of a prune list is exactly how one omission reaches four suites"*; the copies went away and the omission simply moved into whether a caller passes `pruningAtRoot:`. Three tickets have now applied the same point fix. So `CadenceTestTargetHygieneTests.everyWholeTreeWalkOverThisCheckoutPrunesTheRootScratchpad` reads every `CadenceSourceScan.repositoryPaths(` call in the target out of COMMENT-STRIPPED source, balances its argument list, and requires the prune; the fixture walk is the one exemption, named with its reason, and `exempted.count == 1` is asserted so an allowlist cannot grow in silence. Its own needle is spelled in two pieces so it does not count itself. **What that census does NOT cover, said here rather than discovered later: it keys on `repositoryPaths`, so it would not have caught the third fix** -- `CadenceAgentDefaultsIsolationTests` writes its own walk and the census is blind to it, as it would be to the next walk written by hand. It makes the KNOWN shape loud; it is not a detector for whole-tree walks in general. **Two corrections to what the briefs for this work carried.** `scripts/agent-scratch.sh:143` is `local dir="${at:-${TMP_BASE}cadence-${id}-${headsha[1,7]}-$$}"`, so `new <id>` mints OUTSIDE the repository and a tree reaches `scratchpad/` only via `--at`; no guide prescribes `--at` (`docs/AGENT_BRIEF_PREAMBLE.md:25`, `docs/SUBAGENT_RUNBOOK.md:61`, `docs/SUBAGENT_RUNBOOK_REFERENCE.md:29` all give the bare form), so an in-repo tree is a deviation and no documentation fix would address it -- [[T-3330]] was corrected by addendum at `47141c3a` and its fix still stands. And `git status` does NOT hide the probe the way it hides `.claude/worktrees/`: the latter is in `.git/info/exclude`, while `scratchpad/probe-treeprune/` showed as `??` throughout. The silence is practical, not structural -- it was one line among 93 untracked paths. **NOT DONE, deliberately:** `isNestedCheckout` was not widened and `repositoryPaths`' default was not changed; both are costed on [[T-3333]], which is the open question [[T-3330]] left. - [T-3331] **CLOSED 2026-10-21 (coordinator, the commit carrying this line) -- the `cadence-keeper` routine had no self-concurrency guard, and 17 of its last 25 runs started while another keeper was still running.** **Measured, not guessed,** from `list_task_runs` over the 25 most recent runs: peak **3** keepers at once, **8** runs outlived their own 30-minute slot (longest **2h46m**), and 12 finished in under 3 minutes (a keeper with nothing to do exiting early, which is the design working). Concurrent keepers start fresh with no memory and cannot see each other, so they re-triage the same queue, launch agents for the same ticket, and allocate ledger ids independently. **This is the mechanism behind the day's id collisions**: [[T-3310]] and [[T-3311]] each ended up naming two different tickets, which read as a briefing mistake and was really two schedulers allocating in parallel. It also explains repeated test-host-lock queues, since each keeper is entitled to launch up to 3 test-running agents. **FIXED** by a Phase -1 step in the routine's prompt: call `list_task_runs` for `cadence-keeper` first, and if any other run is `running`, report one line and stop before reading a file, launching an agent or pushing. Self-healing, with no lock file to leak -- a crashed run stops being `running` on its own, which a `mkdir` lock would not. **Three stale-prose defects fixed in the same pass.** (a) A hard-coded "known live work -- do not duplicate it" roster named four agents that had all finished and a Codex branch (`codex/block-removal-finish`) that was already SPENT; it is replaced by an instruction to DERIVE live work each run from branches, worktrees and sessions, because any roster written into a prompt is stale within hours. Zoom-aware for free — a shorter hour costs more minutes to protect the same text — and it cannot be tuned away from the thing it protects. **The header was read out of the block, and it is 29pt, not the 32 the ticket warned against assuming.** `TimelineEventBlock.eventBlockBody` is a `VStack(spacing: 2)` of a 9pt-semibold time row over an 11pt-semibold title row inside `TimelineBlockStyle.calendar`'s `.padding(.vertical, 3)`; `NSLayoutManager.defaultLineHeight` reports 11pt and 13pt for those sizes (weight-independent, measured across 7–17pt), so 3 + 11 + 2 + 13 = **29**. `.schedule` pads 4, so the Schedule panel's header is 30pt and one minute of threshold apart; the canvas passes its own style's padding rather than a constant. iOS's `iOSCalendarEventBlock` pads 5, spaces 3 and puts the title first: 5 + 13 + 3 + 11 = **32pt**. `CadenceCalendarOverlapLayoutTests.theLineHeightTableMatchesWhatAppKitReports` walks the table against AppKit so a toolchain that changes the font metrics goes red here rather than quietly moving the threshold, and `theMirroredRowMetricsStillMatchTheTwoEventBlockBodies` pins each number to the literal in the view file. **Both of the owner's clusters, by their literal times.** 2:15–6:15 / 3:00–5:45 / 4:00–6:00 (gaps 45 and 60) come back as one column at depths 0, 1, 2, every block ending on the same trailing edge. 7:00–10:55 / 7:15–10:00 (gap 15) come back as columns 0 and 1 of 2 at depth 0 — equal halves. **The indent rule is a fifth of the width REMAINING to the trailing edge, per step:** `x(depth) = slotWidth * (1 - 0.8^depth)`. Against the owner's measurement off a ~345pt column (0%, ~23%, ~36%) that gives 0%, 20%, **36.0%** — the second step exact, the first three points of percentage inside the stated pixel error. A fraction of the *remainder* rather than of the whole for two reasons: the measured steps shrink (~79pt then ~45pt), which a fixed offset or a fixed fraction of the whole cannot do (both put step two at ~46%), and it can never invert the block however deep the stack goes. Floored at 28pt, the narrowest width at which `TimelineBlockGeometry.handleCapsuleWidth` still returns its full 18. **Where it lives:** `Cadence/Shared/CadenceCalendarOverlapLayout.swift`, pure arithmetic over start/end minutes, because macOS's `TimelineMetricsSupport.computeUnifiedLayouts` and iOS's day column both read it and a second copy is how two surfaces come to disagree about which events overlap. `computeBlockFrame` takes a `cascadeDepth`; depth 0 is byte-for-byte the frame it produced before, pinned by `depthZeroFramesAreUnchangedByTheCascade`. **TASKS AND BUNDLES KEEP EQUAL COLUMNS, and the tradeoff is stated rather than hidden.** `Slot.mayCascade` is false for them, so a task never lays itself over an event and an event never lays itself over a task — a task in a cluster always keeps a column of its own and stays visible. The consequence is that a cascading event is clamped to its own column's trailing edge rather than the canvas's. In a cluster of events alone the column *is* the full usable width, so the screenshot is reproduced either way; the two readings differ only where an event overlaps a task, and there Apple's "run to the day's right edge" would paint over the task. **STILL THE OWNER'S TO RULE ON: whether tasks and bundles should follow events into the cascade** (they are assumed to keep equal columns here), and whether a cascading event should be allowed to cover a task's column after all. **HIT TESTING: found and fixed, not filed.** `TimelineDayCanvas.blockedFrames` (`:358`) rebuilt event rects from `column`/`totalColumns` alone, so an indented block would have reported its *whole* column as occupied and the drag-to-create layer would have refused a drag in a strip the user can see is empty; it passes `cascadeDepth` now. Everything else already read one rect: the block's `frame`, its `.contentShape`, both resize strips and `handleCapsuleWidth`. Draw order is start order and `TimelineScheduledBlocksLayer` renders the events array in order at a single `zIndex`, so the later-starting block is painted on top and — SwiftUI hit-testing topmost first — is the one that answers the click where it covers its predecessor; the slot sort was made stable by construction, because `Array.sort` is not and "which of two blocks starting in the same minute is on top" must not be arbitrary. `TimelineDropInteractionSupport` (Codex-leased) reads only task bundle-shelf frames, always depth 0, and is untouched. One residual, inherent to the design and shared with Apple Calendar: a cascaded block covers its predecessor's bottom resize strip in the overlap region, and the exposed indent (a fifth of the column) is where that strip stays grabbable. **iOS IS NOT A MIRROR, and was worse than macOS.** `iOSCalendarTimelineDayColumn` had **no overlap layout at all**: every event drew at `colWidth - 18` offset 9, so two overlapping events sat exactly on top of one another and the lower one was simply invisible. It reads the same shared solver now — events only; its tasks and bundles still draw full width and stack, exactly as before, so nothing about task/event overlap on that surface changed. A day with no overlapping events keeps the exact width and inset it had. **Mutation-tested on a scratch tree** (`agent-scratch.sh` + `mutate.sh --tree`, never the shared checkout), baseline green over 18 tests, four mutations of the gap comparison and the rules derived from it, all four KILLED and every file restored byte-identically. **Verified:** the new 18-test suite green, 117 tests over 7 adjacent timeline/calendar suites green, macOS build 699 Swift compile tasks and the iOS leg 1398, 0 warnings on both. The `nonisolated`/`Sendable` on `CadenceCalendarOverlapPlacement` and the solver is what cleared the main-actor-isolated `Equatable` conformance warning a sibling picked up off the in-flight file; the baseline is back to 0 over a non-vacuous 443-task run. **[[T-3160]] (paint) is independent and untouched** — no fill, label colour or rail moved here.

  **The sentence is `CadenceReorderVisibility.acrossListsNotice`:** *"Nothing moved — rows only

  landing sentence. It names a **list** and not a sort, which is what makes it safe on every
  surface: `offScreenNotice` may not name a sort because the two surfaces spell the same
  arrangement *Custom* and *List Order*, and "its own list" has one spelling everywhere.
  **The real work is the discrimination, not the string.** `CadenceRowReorderSpan.ownListSiblings`
  answers `nil` for two different events and only one of them is an event: *"nothing was asked
  for"* (drop a row on the row already immediately after it) must stay silent, and *"something was

  the two rows' lists — because a drag can cross a list boundary and still move the row past its
  own siblings, in which case it is a real move and gets the other sentence.

  reading; `adropThatChangesNothingIsNotToldWhyItChangedNothing` is the arm that keeps the sentence
  meaning something. Both public answers are built on one private `sliceMove`, so the two can never
  disagree about what a gesture asked for, and `everyRowRenumberTakesItsSequenceInOrder` follows
  [[T-884]]'s property into it.

  passes a *finished* row on the way, wrote nothing and was told *"Moved, but this sort doesn't
  show it there."* — the exact false claim that type exists to avoid, one surface in. Both
  questions now take the rows the drop renumbers, and
  `thelistTabAsksTheNoticeAboutTheRowsItRenumbers` measures both readings over one arrangement
  rather than asserting the fixed one alone.

- [T-1131] **CLOSED 2026-09-12 (agent `railnow`, verified and landed by `b10land`) — one now-line, and all three timed canvases draw it.** Landed in `e7ecab9`. The repository owner said to build it, and the recommendation it was built to was this entry's own: reuse the Mac's rule rather than invent a second.
  **It is the Mac's overlay, moved rather than ported.** `TimelineCurrentTimeOverlay`'s body is now
  `CadenceTimelineNowLine` in `Cadence/Shared/Components/`, with the arithmetic split into
  `CadenceTimelineNowLineSupport` so the parts that can be wrong are reachable from `CadenceTests`,
  which builds on macOS and compiles none of `Cadence/iOS/`. `TimelineCurrentTimeOverlay` keeps its
  name and its five parameters and is a short adapter from `TimelineMetrics`/`TimelineBlockStyle`,
  so `TimelineDayCanvas` is untouched and nothing the Mac draws changed.
  **The geometry arrives as a closure, not as an hour height**, and that is the load-bearing
  decision. Each canvas hands over *its own* minute-to-Y: the Mac passes
  `metrics.yOffset(forFractionalMinute:)`, iOS's day column passes the `yOffset` every block above
  it already uses, Today's hour row passes a fraction of its own measured height. Taking
  `hourHeight` in shared code instead would have re-created the copy
  `yOffset(forFractionalMinute:)`'s own doc comment warns about — three times over — and would have
  fallen behind iOS's `1x`-`3x` pinch, which is already folded into the `hourHeight` its columns lay
  blocks out with.
  **Today's panel is per hour row rather than one overlay over the pane**, because that grid is a
  flow: a row is `minHeight: rowHeight` and *grows* with the blocks in it, so no expression over
  `rowHeight` locates 13:30 once any hour above 13:00 has something in it. Scoping the rule to the
  row that owns the hour makes the fraction local. It is 24 `TimelineView(.periodic)` leaves rather
  than one pane-level clock deliberately: a pane-level clock would have to invalidate the `ForEach`
  owning all 24 rows, redrawing every block, gesture and lane every 15 seconds, where this redraws
  24 leaves that compute one `dateComponents` and return `EmptyView`. The Calendar grid gates on
  `isDateInToday` at the column so a windowed week does not mint a schedule per column.
  **The dot/no-dot split is the one macOS already had** — Schedule panel yes, Calendar page no —
  and iOS takes the identical split: Today's timeline yes, the windowed Calendar grid no, where one
  dot per visible column would be a row of them across a week.
  **The tick is stated once**, as `CadenceTimelineNowLineSupport.tickInterval` = 15s: macOS's own,
  adopted rather than tightened, because at iOS's resting 58pt hour one minute is 0.97pt, so a
  15-second tick already moves the rule by about a quarter of a point and a tighter one buys
  redraws rather than precision.
  Pinned by five `@Test`s in `CadenceTimelineNowLineTests`: the fractional minute carries its
  seconds and is read in the zone the caller names (one instant, three zones, three answers —
  [[T-1115]]); `isVisible`'s two halves, including that exactly one of Today's 24 one-hour rows
  draws; the rule's origin and far end either side of the dot, and a canvas narrower than its own
  insets asking for zero rather than a negative frame; the interval, against what a tick is worth on
  the densest canvas the app draws; and a population sweep over `Cadence/` built on a
  `CadenceScanInstrument` whose detector is the *conjunction* — a periodic schedule with its
  interval typed beside it — so `iOSFocusView`'s legitimate one-second focus clock is not caught.
  That sweep is registered in `CadenceTests/CadenceRealTreeSweepManifest.txt`.
  **Verified on iOS by building it**, since the macOS test target compiles nothing under
  `Cadence/iOS/`: `generic/platform=iOS Simulator`, 0 errors and 0 warnings, over a non-vacuous
  compile.
  **Originally filed as:** **For the user: should the iOS timed grids get a now-line?** Filed 2026-09-12 by
  `hourladder`, from [[T-619]].
  **What differs.** macOS draws one: `TimelineCurrentTimeOverlay`
  (`Cadence/macOS/Views/TimelineTaskBlockSupportViews.swift:81`) — a 1pt `Theme.red` rule across the
  canvas at the current minute, with an 8pt dot on the Schedule panel, refreshed every 15 seconds by
  `TimelineView(.periodic)`, and drawn only on a column that is actually today. **iOS draws nothing
  of the kind on either timed surface**; the only `TimelineView(.periodic` in `Cadence/iOS/` is the
  focus timer.
  **Why it is filed rather than built.** It is a feature the phone does not have, not a weight that
  drifted — it is the largest of [[T-619]]'s three divergences and the one most likely to read as
  missing rather than as different, since every other calendar app the user has draws one. But it
  is new surface area on a screen that is already dense: iOS's grid scrolls horizontally through a
  windowed day range with columns built on demand, so the line has to be a per-column overlay
  keyed on today rather than one rule across the canvas, and it has to not fight the `1×`–`3×`
  pinch.
  **Recommendation: build it**, reusing the Mac's rule rather than inventing a second — the minute
  arithmetic is already shared-able (`minutesFromMidnight` plus a `yOffset`), and the dot/no-dot
  split the Mac already has is the same choice iOS needs between its grid and Today.

- [T-1130] **CLOSED 2026-09-12 (agent `railnow`, verified and landed by `b10land`) — all four hour rails name the hour through `TimeFormatters`.** Landed in `e7ecab9`. The repository owner chose option 2, *"Both follow the system clock"*.

  **Originally filed as:** **For the user: should the two hour rails say "13" and "1 PM", or one of them?** Filed
  2026-09-12 by `hourladder`, from [[T-619]].
  **Where you see it.** The column of hour labels down the left of every timed grid.
  **What differs.** macOS prints a bare 24-hour integer — `Text("\(hour)")`, at 10pt, in
